title: IHG and Harilela Group announce The Hari's three hotels will join luxury collection brand Vignette Collection
summary: Vignette Collection, Singapore, London, Hong Kong, Harilela Group, The Hari Hotels, hotel signings
body_text: News releases 17 August 2026 IHG and Harilela Group announce The Hari's three hotels will join luxury collection brand Vignette Collection Marks brand entry of Vignette Collection in Singapore and expands presence in Hong Kong and London The Hari London and The Hari Hong Kong joins the Vignette Collection family of luxury hotels this year Holiday Inn Singapore Orchard City Centre will be converted into The Hari Singapore, Vignette Collection in 2027 The Hari London, Vignette Collection download Singapore - 17 August 2026 : IHG Hotels & Resorts (IHG), one of the world’s leading hotel companies, has signed a landmark three-hotel portfolio deal with Harilela Group, a dynamic Hong Kong-based hotel development and management company with a portfolio spanning across Asia and Europe. Under the franchise agreement, the 85-room The Hari London and 210-room The Hari Hong Kong will join IHG’s luxury & lifestyle collection brand, Vignette Collection, alongside the conversion of 324-room Holiday Inn Singapore Orchard City Centre into The Hari Singapore, Vignette Collection . The agreement reflects a partnership that has evolved over more than five decades, with Harilela Group and IHG now collaborating across six hotels. Alongside The Hari portfolio, the relationship includes Holiday Inn Golden Mile in Hong Kong which recently celebrated its 50th anniversary, Holiday Inn Express Changzhou Center and Holiday Inn Bangkok Silom. For Vignette Collection, the addition of three independently spirited hotels, in three global gateway cities, including The Hari’s debut in Singapore, marks an important milestone. These additions strengthen Vignette Collection’s growing presence of over 80 open and pipeline hotels worldwide. As IHG’s luxury & lifestyle collection brand, Vignette Collection brings together distinctive hotels in destinations to remember, united by a shared vision of offering a more authentic way to travel. The Hari Hotels embodies Vignette Collection hallmarks of ‘Memorable Rituals’ and ‘A Means For Good’ in initiatives such as The Hari Art Prize. Rajit Sukumaran, Senior Vice President and Managing Director, East Asia & Pacific, IHG said : “It is a privilege to celebrate more than five decades of partnership with Harilela Group. Since opening Holiday Inn Golden Mile over 50 years ago, we have built a relationship founded on trust, shared ambition and a commitment to delivering exceptional hospitality. “Today’s announcement reaches an exciting new milestone as we extend our portfolio to six hotels in five world class travel destinations, a testament to what we have achieved together. “This landmark agreement introduces Vignette Collection to one of the world’s most strategically important gateway cities and expands its presence in both London and Hong Kong. The Hari Hotels are renowned for their distinctive and understated luxury stays, making them a natural fit for Vignette Collection. We look forward to welcoming guests to these unique hotels when they open.” Dr. Aron Harilela, Chairman and CEO, Harilela Group said: “We have a clear and ambitious vision for The Hari brand with plans to expand its footprint in major international destinations. The Hari Hotels embody a relaxed elegance punctuated by eccentricity, wit, culture and genuine heartfelt hospitality. “Bringing our three The Hari Hotels into Vignette Collection provides a unified brand partnership opportunity, and a powerful platform for growth, combining the hotel’s individuality with the scale, global reach and commercial strength of IHG. We are confident that this partnership will further elevate the guest experience, while driving strong performance and long-term value for our hotels.” Vignette Collection is tracking ahead of the ambition to reach more than 100 hotels within its first decade. Recent openings include The One Shanghai Downtown, Vignette Collection, Palm Springs Hotel Chengdu, Vignette Collection and CIEL Dubai Marina, Vignette Collection, the world’s tallest hotel. Upcoming additions include Mangala Estate Kuantan, Vignette Collection and Vaagali Maldives, Vignette Collection. About The Hari Singapore, Vignette Collection The Hari Singapore, Vignette Collection will be a conversion of the existing 324-room Holiday Inn Singapore Orchard City Centre, which opened in 1985 and is IHG’s longest-operating hotel in Singapore. The hotel is currently undergoing a significant transformation with world-renowned British designer Tara Bernerd, whose portfolio includes The Hari London and The Hari Hong Kong, overseeing the design of the hotel. Located in the heart of Singapore’s renowned Orchard Road precinct and moments from the historic Emerald Hill precinct, the hotel benefits from year-round demand driven by regional leisure travellers, high-spending shoppers, and extended-stay international guests. Its prime location offers excellent connectivity to Marina Bay, Civic District, and Changi Airport. The Hari Singapore, Vignette Collection will welcome guests in 2027. The Hari Singapore, Vignette Collection, Swimming Pool (Rendering) download About The Hari London, Vignette Collection Located in the heart of Belgravia, one of London’s most prestigious and sought-after neighbourhoods, the 85-room The Hari London, Vignette Collection offers a sophisticated residential-style experience. The hotel enjoys proximity to iconic luxury and cultural attractions including Knightsbridge, Sloane Street, and Hyde Park, making it an ideal choice for discerning leisure travellers seeking an intimate stay that is within easy reach of London’s key tourism, retail, and entertainment districts. About The Hari Hong Kong, Vignette Collection The 210-room The Hari Hong Kong, Vignette Collection is situated in Wan Chai, a vibrant and evolving district connecting Causeway Bay and Admiralty. Ideally positioned between the city’s commercial centre and premier leisure and dining precincts, the hotel appeals to both international business and leisure travellers offering a contemporary urban retreat that connects seamlessly to Hong Kong’s leading shopping, cultural, and waterfront attractions. The Hari Hong Kong, Vignette Collection, Exterior download Ends About IHG® IHG Hotels & Resorts (tickers: LON:IHG for Ordinary Shares; NYSE:IHG for ADRs) is a global hospitality company, with a purpose to provide True Hospitality for Good. With a family of 21 hotel brands and IHG One Rewards , one of the world's largest hotel loyalty programmes with over 160 million members, IHG has more than one million rooms across 7,000 hotels in over 100 countries, and a development pipeline of a further 2,400 properties. Luxury & Lifestyle: Six Senses , Regent , InterContinental , Vignette Collection , Kimpton , Hotel Indigo Premium: Noted Collection , voco , Ruby , HUALUXE , Crowne Plaza , EVEN Essentials: Holiday Inn Express , Holiday Inn Hotels & Resorts , Garner , avid Suites: Atwell Suites , Staybridge Suites , Holiday Inn Club Vacations , Candlewood Suites Exclusive Partners: Iberostar Beachfront Resorts InterContinental Hotels Group PLC is the Group's holding company and is incorporated and registered in England and Wales. Approximately 400,000 people work across IHG's hotels and corporate offices globally. Visit us online for more about our hotels and reservations and IHG One Rewards . To download the IHG One Rewards app, visit the Apple App or Google Play stores. For our latest news, visit our Newsroom and follow us on LinkedIn . About Vignette Collection Vignette Collection is IHG’s first collection brand and newest addition to its luxury and lifestyle portfolio. It represents a fast-growing family of unique properties each offering one-of-a-kind stays in destinations to remember. Collectively different and proudly independent, Vignette Collection hotels share the vision to harness travel’s ability to benefit local people and places weaving responsibility, community, and locality together. Since its launch in 2021, the brand has surpassed the halfway point in its initial aim to reach 100 hotels in the first 10 years. Today, the collection encompasses 38 hotels in 17 countries globally with a further 46 properties in the pipeline. Vignette Collection was launched to offer owners of world-class independent hotels the ability to benefit from IHG’s powerful enterprise offering and global scale whilst retaining their hotel’s unique character, style, and name. For more information, visit www.vignettecollectionhotels.com News releases

title: Hospitality from the Heart: Chokchai’s Story
summary: Meet Chokchai, a Bell Captain at Sheraton Grande Sukhumvit in Bangkok, whose thoughtful care helps guests feel welcomed, safe and remembered.
body_text: Name: Chokchai S. Position: Bell Captain Hotel: Sheraton Grande Sukhumvit, A Luxury Collection Hotel, Bangkok, There are hotel moments that announce themselves: the perfect room view, the unforgettable meal, the first glimpse of a beautiful lobby after a long trip. And then there are the quieter moments. The ones that almost pass by unnoticed until later, when you realize they are the reason a place stayed with you. A smile that makes a stranger feel familiar. A few extra minutes of care when no one asked for them. Someone noticing a small worry and stepping in before it becomes a problem. At Sheraton Grande Sukhumvit, A Luxury Collection Hotel, Bangkok, that person is often Chokchai. For more than 20 years, Chokchai has welcomed guests through the hotel’s doors, first as a bellman and later as a bell Captain. His manager, Veera J., describes him as “always ready to assist whenever and wherever he can and with such a strong service mindset.” → Learn About New Career Opportunities at Sheraton Grande Sukhumvit, A Luxury Collection Hotel, Bangkok Veera says Chokchai consistently approaches guests who need assistance and proactively offers support. “He is always willing to go beyond the normal responsibilities of a bellman, helping guests with issues such as jump-starting car batteries, changing flat tires, to packing fragile objects.” Courtesy of Chokchai S. That kind of care is something guests feel quickly. Rich B., a guest from Tennessee who recently stayed at the hotel, remembers meeting Chokchai while he and his wife waited for their Grab rideshare driver. “The second I walked up, he smiled and it felt like we’d known each other for years,” Rich shared. “The driver missed the turn, and Chokchai offered to call and speak to the driver in Thai to help guide him to the hotel. He then stayed with us until the driver picked us up. He went out of his way to help us, and we were so inspired by his kindness and generosity.” For Chokchai, those moments are not about recognition. They are simply part of how he understands hospitality: paying attention, making things easier, and helping people feel looked after. Read more about Chokchai’s authentic hospitality journey, in his own words below. Why did you choose Marriott? One of the reasons I chose to work here was the opportunity to take on the challenge of working for the largest hotel company in the world. Most importantly, the strong sense of friendship and teamwork is what attracted me to the company. My friends who were already working at the Sheraton Grande Sukhumvit invited me to join, and I have enjoyed being part of the team ever since. Courtesy of Chokchai S. What’s your favorite part of your job? Assisting our guests, providing recommendations, and ensuring they enjoy a comfortable and memorable stay. I hope that guests not only remember the Sheraton Grande Sukhumvit for its excellent service but also remember the associates who made their stay special and memorable. “What I do is not just a job or a responsibility. It is something I genuinely love.” CHOKCHAI S. – BELL CAPTAIN What does caring for people mean to you? It is something that has been a part of me since childhood and has become an integral part of who I am. It is paying attention to details and finding ways to make difficult situations easier and more convenient for our guests. What I do is not just a job or a responsibility. It is something I genuinely love. Serving others brings me happiness, and it is a source of motivation and satisfaction in my everyday life. Courtesy of Chokchai S. Looking back in your career, what makes you the proudest? Having the opportunity to mentor and support younger associates who are interested in working as Bellmen. I enjoy teaching them the lessons I have gained in over twenty years, including not only the technical aspects of the job but also the wisdom and problem-solving skills that can only be learned through experience. Helping them grow, develop confidence, and succeed in their careers is extremely rewarding for me. What would you tell someone who is considering joining Marriott? Marriott is more than just a workplace, it is a world-class learning institution for hospitality. It provides the highest standards of training, development, and professional growth. The experience you gain with Marriott is recognized and respected around the world, and it opens doors to opportunities and career growth that can take you far beyond your expectations. If you truly want to understand what makes Marriott special, come and experience it for yourself. Join us, and become part of something extraordinary .

title: Santander Receives Federal Reserve Approval for the Acquisition of Webster Financial Corporation
summary: Banco Santander and Webster Financial Corporation today announced that they have received the required approval from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System for Santander's previously announced acquisition of Webster.
body_text: Communications Santander CEST Linkedin Instagram X Madrid (Spain) and Stamford, CT (USA), August 4, 2026 - PRESS RELEASE Banco Santander, S.A. (“Santander”) and Webster Financial Corporation (“Webster”) today announced that they have received the required approval from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System for Santander's previously announced acquisition of Webster, the holding company for Webster Bank, N.A., a diversified U.S. retail and commercial bank. This follows the approval by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on June 12, 2026, and the authorization granted by the European Central Bank on July 21, 2026. The transaction is now expected to close on August 20, 2026. Santander US and Webster are a perfect match. Together, supported by Santander’s global platforms, technology and expertise, we will create a stronger bank with the scale to better serve our customers and communities. This combination will strengthen our position in one of the world’s most attractive banking markets and put us firmly on track to build one of the highest-performing banks among our U.S. peers. Ana Botín, Executive Chair of Santander We are pleased to be one step closer to this important, strategic acquisition that will expand our scale and round out our U.S. business model. Bringing together these two highly complementary businesses, Santander will be well positioned to better serve our customers and clients, while helping local communities prosper. We are excited for this next chapter for Santander. Christiana Riley, CEO and President of Santander Holdings USA, Inc. (“Santander US”) John Ciulla, Chairman and CEO of Webster , said: “This is an exciting moment that will allow us to soon bring together our two great organizations to benefit our customers and communities. Santander’s expanded scale, enhanced capabilities and financial strength will help us to deepen local relationships and build upon the trusted partnership that Webster customers have come to expect from us.” The transaction is expected to strengthen Santander’s U.S. franchise and accelerate the delivery of its financial objectives. Once integrated, Santander expects its U.S. business to achieve a return on tangible equity (RoTE) of around 18% by 2028, while the transaction is expected to generate approximately 7–8% earnings per share accretion and an estimated 15% return on invested capital, all by 2028. Upon closing, most Webster’s businesses will become part of Santander Bank, N.A., Santander’s banking franchise in the United States. Until the transaction closes, Santander and Webster will continue to operate independently. Customers do not need to take any action at this time, and accounts, products, and services will continue to operate as they do today. Any future changes will be communicated in advance of implementation.

title: Amwell makes grant to new employees under inducement plan
summary: BOSTON, Aug. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Amwell ® (NYSE: AMWL), a leading provider of a comprehensive SaaS-based software platform for technology-enabled healthcare, announces that on August 7, Amwell made grants of RSUs covering an aggregate of 6,679 shares of its Class A common stock to two new
body_text: Amwell makes grant to new employees under inducement plan August 7, 2026 PDF Version BOSTON, Aug. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Amwell ® (NYSE: AMWL), a leading provider of a comprehensive SaaS-based software platform for technology-enabled healthcare, announces that on August 7, Amwell made grants of RSUs covering an aggregate of 6,679 shares of its Class A common stock to two new non-executive employees. The grants were offered as material inducement to the employees’ entry into employment with Amwell. Subject to each employee’s continued employment through the applicable vesting date, 25% of the RSUs will vest on the first anniversary of the grant date (the “Initial Vesting Date”), and the remaining 75% will vest in substantially equal quarterly increments thereafter (subject to rounding for whole shares), beginning on the first calendar day of the month following the date that is three months after the Initial Vesting Date, with the RSUs vesting in full on the first day of the calendar month following the 48-month anniversary of the grant date. The grants described in this press release were approved by the Compensation Committee of the Amwell’s Board of Directors pursuant to American Well Corporation’s 2024 Inducement Plan and made in reliance on the employment inducement exemption under the NYSE Listed Company Manual Rule 303A.08. Amwell is issuing this press release to satisfy the public announcement requirement of Rule 303A.08. About Amwell Amwell offers payers and health systems a single, comprehensive, technology-enabled care platform. We use technology to provide patients with better access to more convenient, affordable and effective care. The Amwell platform includes software and services that power many clinical programs from Amwell and our growing number of partners. Our platform allows patients to experience unified, personalized and simple access to diversified clinical programs across the care continuum. As more people seek care online and more clinical programs become available, we offer integrated, future-ready, consistent solutions. The Amwell platform is proven, operating at a large scale, enabling care for millions of patients and their sponsors while delivering dependable outcomes. For two decades, Amwell has proudly served some of the largest and most sophisticated healthcare organizations in the U.S. and worldwide. For more information, visit business.amwell.com or LinkedIn . Media: Press@amwell.com Investor: Asher Dewhurst amwell@icrhealthcare.com

title: 9 Best voice of customer tools for small businesses
summary: Compare voice of customer tools by channel, pricing, and fit. Find the right VoC software for your small business.
body_text: You already have customer feedback. It shows up in calls, reviews, and support tickets. The data exists… you just don’t have a system that pulls it together. That’s the role of Voice of Customer, or VoC, tools. But most information about collecting data and utilizingVoC tools is written for enterprise companies. This can feel complex for a smaller team. But that’s just not true. There are VoC tools purpose-built for smaller teams. You can start with a single channel and grow from there. Here’s a quick look at what we found: The best Voice of Customer tool for insights from your business phone conversations is Quo . The best Voice of Customer tool for structured surveys is SurveyMonkey . The best Voice of Customer tool for social listening is Brandwatch . The best Voice of Customer tool for omnichannel feedback is Zonka Feedback . Below, we review nine Voice of Customer tools across different categories. Some can get you up and running fast. Others are better suited once you have more feedback volume. What are Voice of Customer tools? Voice of Customer tools collect feedback from channels like phone calls, surveys, and support tickets. These tools can also collect data from public channels like online review sites and social media. Then, they organize the feedback and surface trends, patterns, and themes. To do that, they often rely on AI-powered features like sentiment analysis and customer intelligence . Why do businesses use Voice of Customer software? When you can identify recurring issues across channels, you can fix problems faster. You can also make better decisions about where to invest your resources. 9 Best Voice of Customer tools reviewed and ranked We evaluated each tool on a few key criteria: Channel coverage, or sources of data AI depth Ease of setup and time-to-value Fit for smaller teams For transparency, Quo is our product. We want to call that out as you weigh the information below. Beyond that, every tool was assessed using the same criteria. 9 Best tools for Voice of Customer compared side-by-side Here’s a quick reference of our findings, and you can read more detail in the sections below: Tool Best for Starting price Key features Free trial G2 rating Quo Insights from your business phone conversations $15 per user per month Call/text capture, AI call tags to surface patterns, integrations Seven days 4.7/5 SurveyMonkey Structured surveys $39 per month NPS®/CSAT/CES templates, survey logic Free plan 4.4/5 Jobber Copilot CRM-based VoC $29 per month AI questions on CRM data, job history analysis 14 days 4.6/5 Zendesk Support ticket feedback $55 per user per month Omnichannel ticketing, insights based on customer support 14 days 4.3/5 Brandwatch Social listening Custom pricing Sentiment analysis, competitor monitoring Demo required 4.4/5 Zonka Feedback Omnichannel feedback $49 per month Close the loop with feedback follow up, AI-detected themes Contact sales 4.7/5 Chattermill AI feedback analysis Custom pricing Automated alerts, insights based on customer reviews Demo required 4.4/5 Usersnap Micro-surveys and screen capture $69 per month In-app surveys, annotated screenshots Free tier 4.5/5 Qualtrics XM Complex VoC programs Custom pricing Predictive analytics, NPS/CSAT at scale Demo required 4.4/5 1. Quo: Best Voice of Customer tool for insights from your business phone Pros Gathers call and text data in one organized workspace Shared numbers give every team member visibility into conversations Two-way CRM integration keeps customer data in sync Claude integration lets you turn raw call data into actionable insights Scheduled AI analysis delivers insights to Slack or email AI call tags surface sentiment and themes automatically Detailed call and text analytics Cons Not designed for social, surveys, or web behavior Claude integration requires a Claude Pro or Team plan Every inbound call, missed call, voicemail, and text is a feedback data point. For many small businesses, those data points are never captured or go unreviewed. Quo is a business phone system that captures those interactions in one place. Every plan includes unlimited calling and texting to the US and Canada. On the Business plan, automatic call recording and transcripts make your conversations searchable. The Scale plan adds AI call tags that sort calls by sentiment and topic. You can filter by category and dig into insights by team or time period. Quo’s Claude integration takes this further. After connecting Quo to Claude, you can ask it questions about your call data in natural language. For example, it can find potential causes of issues you’re having. You could ask Claude: “Pull my last 100 messages from [business phone number]. What are customers complaining about the most? Group issues by theme and tell me how many times this topic came up.” You can also set up scheduled Claude tasks. Run a recurring analysis weekly or monthly and deliver results to your inbox. If you prefer Slack or Notion, set Claude up to deliver your results there. By having Claude automatically share a report in your team’s Slack channel, everyone has access to the information. Sign up today for a seven-day free trial and test Quo’s VoC capabilities with your team. Quo pricing Quo offers three pricing plans: Starter: $15 per user per month for unlimited calling and texting in the US and Canada, voicemail transcripts, and more Business: $23 per user per month for call recording, AI call summaries, and CRM integrations Scale: $35 per user per month for AI call tags, detailed analytics, inbound phone support, and a dedicated account manager 2. SurveyMonkey: Best for getting started with structured surveys Pros Fast setup with an intuitive survey builder Limited free plan is available for one user Templates for net promoter score, customer satisfaction, and customer effort score surveys Cons Only captures survey data; doesn’t capture calls, tickets, or reviews Limited AI and theme detection compared to full VoC platforms Limited ability to customize the look and feel of surveys Free plan caps questions at 10 and responses at 25 per survey SurveyMonkey is a survey platform to collect customer feedback. If you’ve never collected structured customer feedback, it’s a solid starting point. You can build a survey in minutes using a template and distribute via email or link, or embed it on your website. Paid plans add skip branching, which are different paths based on question responses. You can also access AI-assisted analysis. But since SurveyMonkey collects survey responses only, you may need a different tool as your VoC needs grow. SurveyMonkey pricing SurveyMonkey has free and paid options available for individual users. The paid tier starts at $46 per month, billed annually. For teams with three or more users, SurveyMonkey has the following plans: Team Advantage: $30 per user per month with a three-seat minimum for unlimited surveys and questions, analyze with AI option, thematic analysis, and the ability to accept payments Team Premier: $92 per user per month with a three-seat minimum for advanced logic, multilingual surveys, and phone support Enterprise: Custom pricing for user management, enhanced security, and premium onboarding 3. Jobber: Best for gathering VoC data from your CRM Pros Surfaces feedback from data a service business already has Answers plain-language questions about clients and jobs inside the CRM Works inside a tool the team uses daily Cons Performance depends on how complete the underlying Jobber data is Won’t analyze calls, reviews, or social feedback Limited reporting capabilities Jobber Copilot is an AI feature inside Jobber , a CRM for home and service-based businesses. You can ask it questions like “Which clients had repeat service requests last quarter?” and it draws answers from your existing records. Copilot works with CRM data within Jobber only. However, you can use the Quo integration to sync your AI-generated call summaries and transcripts to Jobber. That way, you have a more complete picture of the customer interactions . Jobber pricing For a one-person operation, Jobber pricing starts at $29 per month on the Core plan, which covers scheduling, quoting, invoicing, and the client hub. For teams of two to five, Jobber has three plans. AI is available on all plans: Connect: $105 per month for job booking and scheduling, automated reminders, quotes, invoices, and time tracking Grow: $161 per month for advanced quote customizations, automatic time tracking, job costing, and workflow automations, for up to 10 users Plus: $280 per month for access to the marketing suite, premium support, receptionist, and the API walkthrough for custom integrations, for up to 15 users 4. Zendesk: Best for gathering support ticket feedback Pros Pulls email, live chat, and social into one workspace More than 1,000 integrations, including Quo and major CRMs Many AI features are available from the second-tier plan and up 14-day free trial Cons AI sentiment tools require upgrades Per-seat billing and add-ons make the product expensive as your team grows Steeper onboarding and learning curve than single-purpose tools Complex setup for features like advanced routing, triggers, and automations Zendesk is for teams whose main feedback channel comes from support tickets and help center behavior. The Suite plan consolidates email, chat, messaging, and social into one workspace. On the Professional plan, the Admin Copilot can surface personalized insights. Intelligent Triage classifies tickets based on the theme. But for a small team, this is likely not worth the added cost, since the base plan provides usable insights from tickets. Zendesk pricing Zendesk has pricing for Customer Service, Employee Service, and Contact Center teams. Below is pricing for Customer Service: Support Team: $19 per user per month for the email ticketing system with automations and triggers Suite Team: $5 per user per month for AI agents, a knowledge base, and omnichannel routing Suite Professional: $115 per user per month for the AI Admin Copilot, AI App Builder, AI Quick Reports and Intelligent Triage for classifying tickets Suite Enterprise + Copilot: Contact sales for full Intelligent Triage features Zendesk offers the Copilot add-on for a proactive AI assistant to help agents resolve issues faster. It’s $50 per user per month and you must be on the Professional and above. 5. Brandwatch: Best for social listening Pros Search intelligence shows you customer sentiment on almost any topic Social media management features on higher tiers Monitors brand and competitor mentions across platforms Cons No public pricing Some users report that the product is complex and overwhelming Some users report inaccuracies with sentiment analysis Brandwatch finds what people say about your business across social platforms. Then it summarizes themes and sentiment . Two main modules are relevant here. Brandwatch’s Consumer Intelligence platform is for social listening and market research. Social Media Management is for tracking mentions. The platform monitors X/Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, TikTok, and review sites. It can also pick up mentions from the news and blogs. Overall, Brandwatch is most useful once you have social volume worth monitoring. Brandwatch pricing Brandwatch doesn’t have public pricing. All plans require a custom quote. Based on third-party data , costs start at approximately $800 per month. Annual contracts are standard. 6. Zonka Feedback: Best for omnichannel feedback collection Pros Collects feedback via email, SMS, WhatsApp, web, in-app, and kiosks AI flags which issues need attention first Sync your feedback to a CRM or helpdesk for follow up Cons Users report that the software is confusing and sometimes has bugs Slight learning curve for more advanced features May be more platform than smaller teams need initially Zonka Feedback covers collection, analysis, and workflows to close the loop on feedback. A closed-loop action means negative feedback can trigger a follow-up task. From there, teams can stay on top of the resolution. The AI layer groups feedback by theme, scores sentiment, and shows which issues drive the biggest impact. Role-based dashboards give each team member relevant insights. When you’re ready for a full, multi-channel VoC program, Zonka Feedback is a solid choice. Zonka Feedback pricing Zonka Feedback doesn’t publish pricing, but users report that plans start at around $99–$199 per month. AI Feedback Intelligence starts at $799 per month. 7. Chattermill: Best for AI-powered feedback analysis across multiple platforms Pros Wide integration library, including Zendesk, SurveyMonkey, Salesforce, and Forsta AI intelligence automatically tags themes and categorizes sentiment Automated alerts for sudden shifts or spikes in customer feedback Cons Pricing requires a demo and isn’t publicly available Some users report a steep learning curve Some users report inaccurate or unreliable AI insights Chattermill analyzes data from connected tools, such as voice, chat, surveys, and socials. It’s more of an AI analysis layer you add on top of existing tools. It uses deep learning and natural language processing, or NLP, to analyze text and detect themes. You can spot both problems and wins, so you know what to fix and where to double down. You can ask something like “What drove negative sentiment this quarter?” and get an answer based on your connected sources. Chattermill is best for businesses with multiple feedback channels already running. It’s a product you “grow into” rather than start with. Chattermill pricing Chattermill doesn’t publish pricing. A demo call is required. Based on reports , the average annual enterprise contract is approximately $64,000. Pricing depends heavily on your volume of data, data sources, and the features you need. 8. Usersnap: Best for micro-surveys with screen capture tools Pros Build polls and feedback menus directly in a product Keeps user feedback, bug reports, and micro-surveys in a single system Integrations with popular tools like Jira, Zendesk, Slack, and GitHub Cons Limited base plan Some users report that the dashboard is hard to navigate Usersnap lets you create a micro-survey and drop it on your booking page or quote form. You can catch feedback the moment it happens. For example, it lets you collect information about how easy it is for your customers to fill out a contact form, get a quote, or schedule an appointment. If you offer appointment scheduling on your website, you could add a micro-survey that asks: “How easy was it for you to book an appointment today?” Customers can also annotate screenshots to show you if they had a problem — such as a broken dropdown or an unclear field. Usersnap pricing You can collect feedback on 20 items for free. Paid Usersnap plans include: Starter: $49 per month for five users and 15 projects and screen capture widgets to collect feedback Growth: $109 per month for the AI sentiment sensor, reply follow-ups, and an AI sentiment sensor Professional: $189 per month for behavior targeting and segment identification Premium: $369 per month for custom branding and mobile SDK 9. Qualtrics XM: Best for building complex Voice of Customer programs Pros Predictive analytics for feedback programs, often used for in-depth research Covers customer, employee, product, and brand experience AI-powered sentiment analysis with NPS and CSAT tracking Cons Complex implementation requiring dedicated CX resources Steep learning curve for non-technical users No public pricing Qualtrics collects structured feedback across surveys, email, SMS, web, mobile, and contact centers. Its machine learning engine uses predictive analytics to look at customer behavior and predict future events, like churn. Its core strengths are net promoter score, or NPS, and customer satisfaction score, or CSAT, and formal VoC programs. The platform also runs employee and brand experience programs. It’s built for organizations with dedicated CX teams. Mid-market teams consistently report it’s too much for their needs. Qualtrics XM pricing Qualtrics doesn’t publish standard pricing. Based on third-party data , plans may start at around $25,000 per year. A limited free research plan is available for surveys. How do you choose the right VoC tool for your business? Not sure which Voice of the Customer tool is the right fit for your business? There are certainly a lot of options to consider, even beyond the nine tools we’ve covered. A Google search would show you additional options like InMoment, QuestionPro, SentiSum, CustomerGauge, and GetFeedback. But these products target enterprise companies or large B2B organizations. We chose to dig into tools with the widest appeal to small and growing businesses. If you’re exploring your options, run through these five questions to narrow your search: 1. Where does your feedback actually live? Map your channels first. If most interactions happen over the phone, a tool like Quo that captures call analytics gives you more value than a survey platform. Feedback mostly in tickets? Zendesk is a good fit. 2. How much feedback volume do you have? A handful of reviews and a dozen support emails don’t justify an enterprise-grade VoC platform. A CRM-native feature like Jobber Copilot can give you insights into customer satisfaction without a bunch of features you don’t need. 3. Will your team actually use it? A tool nobody logs into doesn’t generate insights. Prioritize platforms that fit workflows you already have, such as Usersnap for app or product feedback. If you use kiosks in your business, then choose Zonka Feedback. 4. Does it integrate with what you already use? Check whether the tool connects to your CRM, phone system, or helpdesk. Customer intelligence software works best when it pushes to and pulls from your daily tools. 5. Does it meet your data privacy requirements? Confirm SOC 2 certification, HIPAA compliance, or GDPR compliance if your business or industry requires it. 6 Features to look for in a VoC tool When evaluating VoC software, check whether the tool has your highest priority features for your budget. Consider: Centralized feedback view. You want one place to see your most important channel sources, whether it’s call data, survey responses, tickets, or reviews. Without it, you’ll miss insights or spend too much time digging for information. AI sentiment and theme detection. Look for automated tagging that sorts feedback by topic and sentiment. You can quickly spot issues, problems, or things your customers appreciate. Scheduled reporting and alerts. You want regular reports delivered to your inbox or Slack without anyone pulling data manually. You won’t have to remember to review the data. Integrations with tools already in use. Data moves automatically between systems. Less manual work means your team is more likely to use the tool consistently and make fewer errors. Analytics dashboard. Visual reporting shows trends over time, conversation analytics , and sentiment breakdowns. The data should be easy to understand so you can act on it. Security and compliance. Look for SOC 2 certification, encryption, role-based access, and industry-relevant regulatory compliance. Turn your customer conversations into your next business decision The right VoC tool gives you a system to capture the data you already have and see what it’s telling you. For a step-by-step guide on putting that feedback to work, check out our voice of customer analysis guide. If most of your customer interactions happen over calls and texts, sign up for a seven-day free trial of Quo . Your conversation data will tell you a lot about your customers. FAQs Do small businesses actually need a VoC tool? Yes. Small businesses collect feedback every day through calls, texts, reviews, and support requests. The difference between acting on that feedback and missing it comes down to having a system. A VoC tool doesn’t have to be complex. Even a phone system with analytics can surface trends that improve the customer experience. What channels should a small business start with for VoC? Start where your feedback already is. For many service businesses, that’s phone calls and texts. Other businesses may rely on social channels or customer support tickets. What are the benefits of Voice of Customer tools for growing businesses? VoC tools help you improve customer satisfaction by identifying issues faster. They can also help you see which services your customers value most. You can better target your marketing by uncovering your most engaged customer segments. When you act on VoC data, you can build customer loyalty, improve customer retention, and reduce customer churn. What are examples of Voice of the Customer? Voice of the Customer data includes any indication of how customers feel. Common Voice of Customer examples include survey responses and feedback forms, NPS, and CES ratings. It may also include call recordings and speech analytics data and support ticket trends. Online reviews and social mentions are another source. Customer interviews and focus groups also count as VoC data. What are the best Voice of Customer tools for small businesses? Quo is the best VoC tool for small businesses whose interactions happen over calls and texts. SurveyMonkey works well for gathering structured survey feedback. Jobber Copilot suits service businesses already using Jobber as their CRM. Are there free or low-cost Voice of Customer tools? SurveyMonkey has a free plan with basic survey capabilities to collect direct feedback. Usersnap offers a free tier for up to 20 feedback items. Starting with a free plan is a practical way to start looking at VoC data without a commitment.

title: Goldman Sachs Announces Agreement to Acquire NEOS Investments
body_text: Acquisition will add $30 billion in active income ETFs to Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s $40 billion in income and outcome-oriented options-based ETF solutions Combined platform will position Goldman Sachs Asset Management as a top eight active ETF provider with $80 billion in active ETFs across a $130 billion global ETF platform as of June 30, 2026 Acquisitions of NEOS Investments and Innovator Capital Management, combined with Goldman Sachs Asset Management, create broad options-based ETF franchise NEW YORK – August 12, 2026 – The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (Goldman Sachs) (NYSE: GS) today announced it has entered into an agreement to acquire NEOS Investments (NEOS), a specialized provider of systematic options-based income exchange-traded funds (ETFs). NEOS, one of the fastest-growing ETF platforms, manages $30 billion in assets across 19 options-based income ETFs as of June 30, 2026. Through this acquisition, Goldman Sachs Asset Management expands its offering of sophisticated derivative-based ETF solutions to help meet the growing demand and broad range of global portfolio needs for investors and advisors. “As investor demand for active ETFs grows, NEOS’ disciplined investment approach is highly complementary to our capabilities across buffer, managed outcome and income strategies. Together, we will give investors a diverse toolkit for different market environments,” said David Solomon, Chairman and CEO of Goldman Sachs. “NEOS’ innovative ETF solutions and intuitive financial education programs have helped them build a strong market presence across a diverse investor base and this acquisition is an excellent strategic and cultural fit.” Growth in derivative income ETFs has accelerated as investors expect modern solutions to deliver attractive income, navigate interest rate volatility and manage risk in the transparent, tax-efficient ETF wrapper. Industry-wide, derivative income ETFs have grown to approximately $180 billion in assets under management (AUM) and represent one of the fastest-growing categories of ETFs, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of more than 70% since 2021, according to Morningstar. NEOS has been one of the market leaders in the derivative income category since launching its flagship options-based income ETF suite in 2022. “Our vision for NEOS since our founding has been to meet investors where they are, challenge conventional thinking and develop innovative investment solutions that aim to help achieve better outcomes. Every investor’s income needs, risk tolerances and objectives are unique, and we built our business with that core understanding. Our commitment to that principle is absolute,” said Garrett Paolella, Co-Founder of NEOS . “As we think about the next chapter for our business, Goldman Sachs Asset Management is a partner that shares our commitment to investment excellence and innovation. Together, we’ll combine NEOS’ entrepreneurial spirit with Goldman Sachs’ scale, expertise and resources to expand the reach of NEOS’ solutions and deliver even greater value for our investors,” said Troy Cates, Co-Founder of NEOS. Founded in 2022, NEOS is a pioneer in next-generation options-based ETF solutions that seek to provide high monthly income, tax efficiency and diversification. As of June 30, 2026, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Innovator from Goldman Sachs Asset Management and NEOS manage more than $130 billion in ETF assets under supervision (AUS). The combination will create the eighth largest active ETF manager as of June 30, 2026, according to Morningstar. With complementary sales and marketing capabilities, we believe there are significant opportunities to grow the firm’s overall ETF franchise as wealth demand continues to grow globally. NEOS’ investment capabilities expand Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s leadership in seeking to deliver attractive investment performance and exceptional service to its clients. Goldman Sachs Asset Management offers a broad range of Direct Indexing and separately managed accounts, active ETFs and alternative investment strategies including through its G-Series evergreen funds. The partnership seeks to provide NEOS the scale and resources to strengthen its brand and ability to serve investors in new markets, while preserving the firm’s distinct philosophy. Following the completion of the transaction, Co-Founders and Managing Partners Troy Cates and Garrett Paolella, pioneers in the options-based ETF industry, will join Goldman Sachs Asset Management as Partners. They bring decades of expertise in options-based investing to advance Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s leadership in active ETFs, tax-efficient income strategies and investment solutions. Upon completion of the transaction, it is expected that the full NEOS team will join Goldman Sachs Asset Management, including founders, investors, and client service teams. The acquisition strategically expands the firm’s more durable revenue and reinforces its commitment to offering investors comprehensive solutions. The transaction consideration of up to $2.25 billion in cash and equity is subject to the achievement of certain performance and/or service commitments. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions. Goldman Sachs was advised by Goldman Sachs Global Banking & Markets as financial advisor and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and Willkie Farr & Gallagher LLP as legal counsel. Barclays is serving as exclusive financial advisor and Ropes & Gray LLP is serving as legal counsel to NEOS. About Goldman Sachs Goldman Sachs is a leading global financial institution that delivers a broad range of financial services to a large and diversified client base that includes corporations, financial institutions, governments and individuals. Founded in 1869, the firm is headquartered in New York and maintains offices in all major financial centers around the world. About Goldman Sachs Asset Management Goldman Sachs Asset Management is the primary investing area within Goldman Sachs, delivering investment and advisory services across public and private markets for the world’s leading institutions, financial advisors, and individuals. The business is driven by a focus on partnership and shared success with its clients, seeking to deliver long-term investment performance drawing on its global network and deep expertise across industries and markets. Goldman Sachs Asset Management is a leading investor across fixed income, liquidity, equity, alternatives, and multi-asset solutions. Goldman Sachs oversees approximately $4 trillion in assets under supervision as of June 30, 2026. Follow us on LinkedIn . Assets Under Supervision (AUS) includes assets under management and other client assets for which Goldman Sachs does not have full discretion. About NEOS Investments Founded in 2022, NEOS Investments offers ETFs that aim to deliver the next evolution of options strategies, where seeking income is the outcome. Built on decades of research and experience, NEOS ETFs aim to empower investors with portfolio building blocks that provide monthly income, tax efficiency, and diversification through data-driven options-based ETFs. NEOS Investments’ shareholder base includes Aretex Capital and investor Tom Lydon. title: Kadant Black Clawson Starts Up New Green Liquor System at Södra Cell Mörrum
summary: Kadant successfully starts up a new green liquor system at Södra’s Mörrum mill, boosting efficiency, chemical recovery, and sustainability.
body_text: LEBANON, Ohio — August 10, 2026 — Kadant Black Clawson LLC, a subsidiary of Kadant Inc. (NYSE: KAI), recently announced the successful startup of a new green liquor system at Södra’s mill in Mörrum, Sweden. Kadant Black Clawson, in collaboration with Kadant Noss AB, developed the system following a detailed evaluation of the mill’s operating environment to meet site-specific process requirements while supporting long-term sustainability and profitability objectives. The solution upgrades Södra’s green liquor processing with the installation of a green liquor clarifier (GLC) and a dregs precoat filter (DPF). The GLC is designed to handle 100 liters per second and delivers high-quality green liquor, with dregs efficiently removed by the DPF. Kadant’s green liquor clarifier features the Uniform Flow Design feedwell and Uniform Liquor Removal bustle pipe, producing ultra-clean green liquor while reducing capital and operating costs. By lowering dregs dead load in both liquor and mud circuits, the design improves recausticizing efficiency and reduces energy consumption. Kadant’s dregs precoat filter recovers green liquor from the clarifier underflow while producing a low-moisture, low-chemical cake that is environmentally non-hazardous and suitable for landfill disposal. Together, the system delivers high filtration capacity, efficient chemical recovery, and cost savings for the mill. “Kadant’s high-efficiency solution supports our growing production goals and delivers the level of performance we need to remain competitive in an increasingly challenging market,” stated Leif Sjöblom, strategic purchaser investments at Södra. Södra selected the Kadant recausticizing solution following a comprehensive evaluation of available technologies. The project included site-specific engineering and end-to-end maintenance support, leveraging Kadant’s extensive experience and long-standing Goslin legacy in chemical pulp recausticizing systems. About Södra Södra was founded in 1938 and is the largest forest-owner association in Sweden. The company processes forest raw material into renewable products such as pulp, timber, building systems, energy and biochemicals. Södra’s mill in Mörrum is a specialized pulp mill with two production lines—one producing premium paper pulp and the other dissolving pulp for textile and specialty applications. The mill has an annual production capacity of 470,000 tons and employs approximately 400 people. About Kadant Black Clawson LLC Kadant Black Clawson LLC is a leading supplier of fiber processing and recycling equipment, designing, manufacturing, and servicing systems used in virgin and recycled stock preparation and paper machine approach-flow applications. The company’s technologies and services enhance process efficiency, optimize energy utilization, and maximize productivity in resource-intensive industries. For more information, visit fiberprocessing.kadant.com About Kadant Noss AB Kadant Noss AB is a leading supplier of fiber processing equipment and systems, providing innovative solutions for chemical and mechanical pulp applications, as well as approach flow applications for paper, board, and tissue machines. The company offers design, engineering, project management, and service for complete systems used in cleaning, fractionation, thickening, screening, deaeration, and other fiber processing applications. For more information, visit fiberprocessing.kadant.com About Kadant Inc. Kadant Inc. is a global supplier of technologies and engineered systems that drive Sustainable Industrial Processing®. The Company’s products and services play an integral role in enhancing efficiency, optimizing energy utilization, and maximizing productivity in process industries. Kadant is based in Westford, Massachusetts, with approximately 4,000 employees in 22 countries worldwide. For more information, visit kadant.com . title: Why Loyalty Programs Work For Liquor Stores
summary: An honest look at loyalty programs for liquor stores, including how they work, what they improve, and whether they’re worth implementing.
body_text: A loyalty program is a structured way to reward customers for repeat purchases. The idea behind every loyalty program is simple: the more a customer shops with you, the more value they receive in return. That value can come in the form of points, discounts, store credit, free items, or exclusive perks. One of the earliest large-scale loyalty programs dates back to 1896, when S&H Green Stamps were introduced in the United States. Retailers gave customers stamps based on how much they spent, and those stamps could later be redeemed for household goods from a catalog. The gist of it remains the same to this day, and here’s how it applies in liquor retail: The Basics of Loyalty Programs for Liquor Stores In liquor retail, loyalty programs usually (but not always) revolve around spending. A customer earns something based on how much they spend, and once they reach a threshold, they receive a reward. Here’s an example: Earn 1 point for every $1 spent Redeem 500 points for $5 off In that setup, a customer who spends $500 earns a $5 reward. From the customer’s perspective, purchases are “adding up.”, while from the store’s perspective, the reward cost is predictable and modest. The exact structure of a loyalty program is less important than how clearly it is communicated. Customers should not have to think or ask questions to understand how it works. They should immediately know how they earn rewards, what those rewards are worth, and when they can use them. In other words, if the program requires explanation every time, it is too complicated. Why Loyalty Programs Matter More for Independent Liquor Stores Loyal Customers Visit More Often Because even a modest reward can influence behavior, customers are more likely to stop by “their” store for a midweek bottle or an unplanned purchase when they know it moves them closer to a reward. This increases visit frequency without needing constant discounts or advertising spend. Customers Will Also Spend More Per Visit Loyalty programs often increase average basket size because they give customers a clear reason to spend a little more each time they shop. When a customer is close to earning a reward, they start thinking in terms of “how do I get this reward faster?” rather than “what is the cheapest thing I can buy today?” That mindset shift encourages them to add an extra bottle, try a new brand, or pick a premium option they might otherwise skip. Research shows that loyalty program members spend 12–18% more annually than non-members, which means stores earn more from the same customers over time. Retention Is More Profitable Than Acquisition Bringing in new customers almost always costs more than keeping the ones you already have. New shoppers need to be convinced to walk through the door, compare prices, and trust your store enough to make a purchase, and that usually requires advertising, promotions, or discounts, all of which eat into margins before you see any long-term return. Repeat customers already know your location, your staff, and the kind of selection you carry, so they walk into the store with intent rather than hesitation. Because they trust your store, they are more willing to try new products, and less likely to shop purely on price. Loyalty programs reinforce this behavior by giving customers a concrete reason to keep choosing your store instead of drifting between options. Loyalty Programs Create Customer Insight Each time a customer shops using a loyalty program, you learn something about how they buy. You start to see clear differences in behavior, such as: Customers who buy wine every week Customers who shop less often but spend more when they do Customers who mainly buy craft beer versus those who focus on spirits. Customers who respond to discounts versus those who consistently buy at full price. This information gives you a clearer picture of what actually moves in your store and who it moves with, which in turn makes it easier to run promotions that align with real buying behavior. Common Loyalty Program Structures That Work Now that we’ve covered why loyalty programs work, let’s talk about how you can structure your own. Below are the most common loyalty program formats used by independent liquor retailers: Points-Based Rewards This is the most straightforward model which we’ve covered in the first section of the article. It works because it is easy to explain and easy to scale, while also allowing flexibility. Once the core rules are in place, the same structure also gives you room to layer in short-term incentives, such as bonus points on specific days or categories, without changing how the program works at its foundation. Spend-and-Get Rewards Some stores frame rewards as spend thresholds. For example: Spend $100, get $5 off Spend $250, get $15 off This structure feels concrete to customers who may not like thinking in points. It also makes reward value immediately obvious. Visit-Based Rewards This model flips the logic of spend-and-get rewards. It focuses on encouraging customers to return more often, regardless of how much they spend on each visit, rather than pushing higher spend in a single transaction. For example, you can reward a customer with store credit after a set number of visits, or offer a free bottle after they’ve purchased a certain number of bottles. The value accumulates through consistency rather than higher-priced purchases. Tiered Loyalty Programs Tiered programs build on the basic loyalty structures above by adding progression. While points-based and spend-and-get programs reward everyone the same way, tiered programs recognize that not all customers contribute equally over time. Instead of offering a single set of rewards, you group customers into levels based on how much or how often they shop with you. Entry-level members earn standard rewards, while higher-tier customers receive added benefits, such as faster point accumulation or exclusive pricing. This approach works best when you already have a base of regular customers and want to give your top spenders a reason to consolidate more of their purchases with your store. It introduces a sense of status and progression that simple earn-and-redeem programs do not, but it also requires clearer rules and more consistent tracking to avoid confusion. Addressing the Common Concerns While the data clearly shows that loyalty programs work, some liquor store owners are still hesitant to implement them. The hesitation is understandable, but when you look at the long-term impact on repeat business and customer value, not having a loyalty program often costs more than running one. Here are the most common concerns, along with some important context that often gets overlooked. “I Can’t Afford to Give Discounts” A loyalty program is often mistaken for blanket discounting, but that is not how effective programs work. You control exactly how generous the rewards are, and in most successful liquor stores, rewards account for roughly 1–2 percent of total sales. That cost is typically recovered through more frequent visits and slightly larger baskets over time. Just as importantly, rewards are only earned after customers spend money with you. You are not giving anything away upfront or discounting hypothetical purchases. You are rewarding real, completed transactions that already contribute to revenue. “It Sounds Complicated to Manage” When loyalty programs feel complicated, the issue is usually not the concept itself, but how it is implemented. With the right setup, loyalty should be embedded into the checkout process so it runs in the background rather than adding another task for you or your team. “My Staff Is Already Busy” Staff workload is a legitimate concern, because loyalty programs only work if they do not slow the line or complicate checkout. The most effective programs are customer-led and take only a few seconds to engage with. Staff involvement should be limited to a brief mention, while the system itself handles enrollment, tracking, and rewards automatically. How Santé POS Helps You Run Loyalty the Right Way Running a loyalty program effectively requires a system that connects purchases, customer profiles, and rewards without adding operational overhead. Santé POS was built specifically for independent liquor stores and includes loyalty functionality designed to support the exact strategies outlined in this article. With Santé POS, each purchase is tied to a customer profile , which means you are not just tracking points, but actually seeing how people shop over time. You can tell what they buy, how often they come in, and how their habits change, all without pulling reports from multiple tools. The same loyalty logic applies whether someone shops in your store or online. Customers earn and redeem rewards across both channels, so there is no disconnect between in-store behavior and online activity, and no confusion about where points “count.” Because purchase history lives in one place, promotions can be based on what customers actually buy, and not broad assumptions. Instead of sending the same discount to everyone, you can run offers that make sense for specific groups of customers. Most importantly, none of this requires manual tracking. Points, rewards, and redemptions are handled automatically, which reduces errors, keeps checkout moving, and removes yet another task from your staff’s plate. Santé POS is designed to support retention, personalization, and repeat business without complicating day-to-day operations. If you want to see how loyalty programs can actually drive growth for your store, you can schedule a demo and see how Santé POS supports loyalty, marketing, and customer engagement in one unified system.

title: Data Center Networking: Architecture, Infrastructure, Topologies, and Best Practices

body_text: Data center networking is the communication framework that connects servers, storage systems, switches, routers, security appliances, and external networks inside a data center. Data center networking supports application delivery, storage access, virtualization, cloud computing, and distributed workloads across enterprise, colocation, hyperscale, and edge facilities. High-speed Ethernet (10 GbE, 25 GbE, 100 GbE, 400 GbE, 800 GbE), Internet Protocol (IPv4, IPv6), Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs), and Software-Defined Networking (SDN) maintain reliable communication with low latency and high bandwidth. Modern deployments support artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, database clusters, and containerized applications that require continuous connectivity and predictable traffic flow. Data center networking combines network architecture, physical infrastructure, virtual networking, topology, switching, routing, and security into a unified communication environment. Leaf-spine architecture, redundant network paths, load balancing, and automated traffic management improve scalability and network resilience under increasing workloads. Physical devices (switches, routers, firewalls, network interface cards, optical transceivers) operate alongside virtual technologies (network virtualization, SDN, overlay networks) to improve resource utilization and simplify management. Structured network design, continuous monitoring, redundancy planning, and standardized protocols reduce latency, improve availability, and maintain consistent application performance across modern IT environments. What Is Data Center Networking? Data center networking is the communication framework that connects servers, storage systems, networking hardware, virtualization platforms, and external networks inside a data center. The framework transports application traffic, storage traffic, management traffic, and internet traffic through high-speed, low-latency connections that maintain continuous service availability. Traditional enterprise networking focuses on user devices, office locations, and branch connectivity. Data center networking focuses on high bandwidth, east-west traffic, workload mobility, storage performance, and application reliability across densely connected computing environments. Modern deployments rely on Ethernet, Internet Protocol, Virtual Local Area Networks, Software Defined Networking, network virtualization, and redundant switching to support cloud computing, artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and large-scale business applications. Network architecture emphasizes scalability, resilience, fault tolerance, and automated traffic management through structured physical and virtual connectivity. Redundant communication paths reduce downtime, and centralized management platforms simplify configuration, monitoring, and policy enforcement across thousands of connected devices. Clear knowledge of networking concepts supports a broader understanding of what is data center within modern computing environments. What Are the Core Components of a Data Center Network? The core components of a data center network are hardware and software that provide connectivity, traffic forwarding, security, and centralized management. Each component performs a dedicated function that supports reliable communication across computing resources. Modern deployments combine physical devices and software platforms to improve scalability, resilience, and application performance. Coordinated operation maintains stable network services under demanding workloads. The core components of a data center network are listed below. Switches : Switches forward Ethernet frames across local network segments by using Media Access Control addresses. Leaf, spine, and Top of Rack switches provide high bandwidth connectivity from 10 Gbps to 800 Gbps. Routers : Routers forward Internet Protocol packets across different networks through routing tables and dynamic routing protocols. External connectivity, wide-area communication, and cloud connections depend on routing functions. Network Interface Cards (NICs) : Network Interface Cards connect servers and storage systems to the network. Modern adapters support speeds from 1 Gbps to 800 Gbps and technologies (RDMA, SR IOV, hardware offloading). Firewalls : Firewalls inspect and filter network traffic according to security policies. Stateful inspection, deep packet inspection, and access control reduce unauthorized communication. Load Balancers : Load balancers distribute application requests across multiple servers. Balanced traffic improves response time and application availability during peak demand. Cables and Optical Transceivers : Copper cables, fiber optic cables, and optical transceivers transmit data across network links. Fiber optic infrastructure supports higher bandwidth and longer transmission distances than copper. Network Management Platforms : Network management platforms monitor network health, collect telemetry, automate configuration, and analyze performance metrics. Centralized visibility improves operational control across large environments. How Does a Data Center Network Work? A data center network works through coordinated communication across servers, storage systems, switches, routers, security appliances, and management platforms. Applications generate network traffic that passes through Network Interface Cards before reaching access switches. Leaf switches forward traffic directly to destination devices or spine switches through low-latency paths. Routers transfer Internet Protocol traffic across external networks through dynamic routing protocols. Firewalls inspect inbound and outbound traffic before communication reaches protected resources. Load balancers distribute client requests across multiple application servers to prevent resource congestion. Virtual networks isolate workloads through software controls without requiring dedicated physical hardware. Software-Defined Networking centralizes policy management and programs forwarding behavior across network devices. Redundant links and redundant switches maintain communication during hardware failures or maintenance events. Continuous monitoring collects latency, throughput, interface utilization, packet loss, and error statistics that support stable operation across enterprise workloads, cloud platforms, artificial intelligence clusters, and high-performance computing environments. Why Is Data Center Networking Important? Data center networking is important because reliable communication determines application performance, system availability, data accessibility, and business continuity across modern computing environments. High-speed network connectivity transfers information from servers to storage systems, cloud platforms, users, and external services with minimal latency and packet loss. Redundant network paths reduce service interruptions during hardware failures, scheduled maintenance, or unexpected network events. Scalable network architecture supports increasing workloads without creating communication bottlenecks that reduce application responsiveness. Software-Defined Networking, network virtualization, and automated traffic management simplify administration across thousands of connected devices. Strong network security protects sensitive information through firewalls, access controls, network segmentation, and encrypted communication. Continuous monitoring identifies congestion, hardware faults, interface errors, and abnormal traffic patterns before performance degradation affects production systems. Reliable networking supports enterprise applications, financial systems, healthcare platforms, manufacturing operations, artificial intelligence training, and cloud computing services that require uninterrupted connectivity, predictable performance, and resilient infrastructure. What Is Network Infrastructure? Network infrastructure is the collection of physical hardware, communication media, software platforms, and network services that enable data transmission across connected systems. The infrastructure connects servers, storage arrays, user devices, cloud resources, and internet gateways through structured communication paths that support reliable information exchange. Core hardware (switches, routers, firewalls, load balancers, network interface cards) manages traffic forwarding, routing, security, and workload distribution. Communication media (fiber optic cables, copper cables, optical transceivers) carry network signals across short and long distances with defined bandwidth and latency characteristics. Modern network infrastructure incorporates Software Defined Networking, network virtualization, centralized management platforms, and automated policy enforcement to simplify administration and improve operational consistency. Redundant devices, redundant links, and redundant power systems maintain service availability during equipment failures or maintenance activities. Continuous monitoring measures throughput, latency, packet loss, interface utilization, and hardware health to maintain stable network performance. Structured network infrastructure supports enterprise applications, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and large-scale storage environments through secure, scalable, and resilient connectivity.

(Nasdaq: HALO) ("Halozyme") today announced the election of Dannielle Appelhans to its Board of Directors. Ms. Appelhans brings more than 20 years of executive leadership across the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries, with deep expertise in operations, manufacturing, and supply chain management. "Dannielle brings a rare combination of operational excellence and manufacturing depth that aligns directly with our growth strategy, and we are delighted to welcome her to the Halozyme board," said Dr. Helen Torley, President and Chief Executive Officer. "As we continue to scale ENHANZE as a compounding platform engine and advance Hypercon and Surf Bio, her experience transforming global operations and executing major partnerships will be a tremendous asset as we deliver on our growth strategy and create meaningful new value for our partners, patients, and shareholders." Ms. Appelhans has served as President and Chief Executive Officer of COUR Pharmaceuticals, a private biotechnology company developing platform-based therapies for autoimmune diseases, since 2023. Under her leadership, the company negotiated and executed a strategic collaboration with Genentech with a potential value of up to $1 billion. Previously, she served as Chief Executive Officer of Rubius Therapeutics, Inc., a publicly traded, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company. Earlier, she held roles of increasing responsibility at Novartis, culminating as Senior Vice President and Chief Technical Officer of Novartis Gene Therapies, where she led development, manufacturing, and supply chain for the gene therapy unit, including the approved therapy Zolgensma, and as Senior Vice President, Global Head of Supply Chain Management. She began her career at McKinsey & Company and Eli Lilly and Company, and previously served on the Board of Directors of Generation Bio Co. "I am honored to join Halozyme's Board of Directors," said Ms. Appelhans. "Halozyme has built a differentiated, royalty-driven business and a compelling strategy for durable growth through its multiple drug delivery technology platforms. I look forward to working with the board and leadership team to help deliver even greater value to patients and shareholders." Ms. Appelhans earned a Master of Science in mechanical engineering from Massachusetts Institute of Technology's School of Engineering, an MBA from Massachusetts Institute of Technology's Sloan School of Management, and a Bachelor of Science in mechanical engineering from the University of Michigan. About Halozyme Halozyme is a biopharmaceutical company advancing disruptive solutions to improve patient experiences and outcomes for emerging and established therapies. As the innovators of ENHANZE® drug delivery technology with the proprietary enzyme rHuPH20, Halozyme's commercially-validated solution facilitates the subcutaneous delivery of injected drugs and fluids, reducing treatment burden and improving convenience. ENHANZE® has touched more than one million patient lives through ten commercialized products across over 100 global markets and is licensed to leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies including Roche, Takeda, Pfizer, Janssen, AbbVie, Eli Lilly, Bristol-Myers Squibb, argenx, ViiV Healthcare, Chugai Pharmaceutical, Acumen Pharmaceuticals, Merus N.V., Skye Bioscience, GSK and Incyte. Halozyme expanded its drug delivery technology portfolio to develop partner products using Hypercon™ and Surf Bio's hyperconcentration technology. Hypercon™ is an innovative microparticle technology expected to set a new standard in hyperconcentration of drugs and biologics by reducing injection volume for the same dosage and enabling administration in at-home and healthcare-provider settings. The addition of Surf Bio's polymer-based hyperconcentration technology further broadens the range of biologics that can be delivered subcutaneously, meaningfully expanding the scope of opportunities across therapeutic modalities. Together, Hypercon™ and Surf Bio's technology complement ENHANZE® by enabling creation and delivery of highly concentrated biologics. The Hypercon™ technology has been licensed to leading biopharmaceutical partners, including Janssen, Eli Lilly, argenx, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, and Oruka Therapeutics. Halozyme also develops, manufactures and commercializes drug-device combination products using advanced auto-injector technologies designed to improve convenience, reliability and tolerability, enhancing patient comfort and adherence. The Company has two proprietary commercial products, Hylenex® and XYOSTED®, partnered commercial products and ongoing development programs with Teva Pharmaceuticals and McDermott Laboratories Limited, an affiliate of Viatris Inc. Halozyme is headquartered in San Diego, CA, with offices in Ewing, NJ; Minnetonka, MN; and Boston, MA. Minnetonka is also the site of its operations facility.
