title: Top Providers for Multi-Lender Underwriting Orchestration in 2026
summary: Multi-lender underwriting orchestration connects borrower data, credit decisioning, and multiple lending partners in one workflow. Instead of building separate integrations and underwriting processes for every lender, businesses can use an orchestration layer to evaluate an application, determine which lenders fit, route the deal, and manage the response from one system.
body_text: The challenge is that not every underwriting platform provides true multi-lender orchestration. Some specialize in credit decisioning. Others focus on data or workflow automation. A smaller group combines underwriting infrastructure with the ability to route applications across an actual lender network. Below, we'll compare the top providers for multi-lender underwriting orchestration, where each platform fits, and what to look for when choosing one. What Is Multi-Lender Underwriting Orchestration? Multi-lender underwriting orchestration is the process of coordinating borrower evaluation and application routing across multiple lenders through a centralized technology layer. A borrower submits one application. The platform collects and normalizes the required data, evaluates the borrower against underwriting criteria, and determines which lenders or credit products are appropriate. From there, applications can be routed sequentially or simultaneously based on factors like credit profile, revenue, industry, requested amount, product type, lender appetite, and other eligibility requirements. The core components typically include: Data aggregation: Pulling borrower, banking, credit, identity, and business data into a standardized format Decisioning: Applying eligibility rules and underwriting logic to determine borrower fit Lender matching: Identifying lenders whose credit boxes align with the application Routing: Sending qualified applications to the appropriate lenders automatically Workflow automation: Managing documents, status changes, exceptions, and communications Offer management: Returning and presenting lender decisions or offers through a unified experience The result is a lending workflow that can support multiple capital providers without requiring the operator to manually manage every lender relationship and application handoff. Top Multi-Lender Underwriting Orchestration Providers The right platform depends heavily on what you're trying to orchestrate. Some businesses need access to a ready-made lender network. Others already have capital partners and primarily need a configurable decision engine. Enterprise lenders may instead prioritize sophisticated risk policies, data integrations, and governance. Here are the leading providers to consider. 1. Lendflow Lendflow is built specifically for businesses that need to connect underwriting, workflow automation, and multiple lending partners within one infrastructure layer. Rather than requiring teams to integrate separately with every lender, Lendflow Connect provides access to a network of 75+ specialty and bank lenders through a centralized integration. Applications can be matched and routed based on borrower characteristics and lender criteria. Lendflow also combines orchestration with data and decisioning infrastructure. That means businesses can collect borrower information, analyze documents, configure underwriting logic, and route qualified applications without stitching together a separate platform for every stage. Best for: Fintechs, brokers, vertical SaaS platforms, marketplaces, and embedded finance companies that want both underwriting infrastructure and access to multiple lenders. Key capabilities: Network of 75+ lenders Multi-lender application routing Configurable underwriting and decisioning Borrower data aggregation AI-powered document analysis Workflow automation API, widget, and hosted deployment options Unified borrower experience Lender and funnel analytics The biggest distinction is that Lendflow combines the orchestration technology with an existing lender ecosystem. Businesses that don't already have dozens of lender relationships can use the same infrastructure to solve both problems. 2. Taktile Taktile is a decisioning platform designed to help financial institutions build, test, and optimize automated decision strategies. Its visual decision environment allows risk teams to configure underwriting logic without hard-coding every policy change into the core product. Teams can connect third-party data, create rules, test strategies against historical data, and experiment with different decision flows. That makes Taktile useful when the primary problem is underwriting orchestration rather than lender-network access . Best for: Fintechs and financial institutions that already have lending or capital relationships and want flexible control over credit decisioning. Key capabilities: Visual decision workflows Low-code underwriting logic Third-party data integrations Simulation and testing A/B testing Real-time analytics AI-assisted workflow development Taktile can act as a flexible decision layer inside a multi-lender architecture, but organizations generally need to supply and manage the surrounding lender integrations themselves. 3. Provenir Provenir provides enterprise credit decisioning and data orchestration for financial services companies. The platform combines configurable decision logic with access to a large marketplace of external data providers. Provenir says its marketplace includes more than 120 data partners covering areas such as credit, fraud, identity, open banking, and alternative data. That makes it particularly useful for organizations operating complex underwriting strategies across markets or products. Best for: Larger financial institutions and fintechs that need enterprise-grade decisioning, data orchestration, and governance. Key capabilities: Real-time credit decisioning Configurable decision workflows Global data marketplace 120+ data partners Single-API data access Fraud and identity data Version-controlled decision strategies Enterprise compliance controls Like Taktile, Provenir is primarily a decisioning and data platform rather than a pre-built network of lenders. Businesses building multi-lender workflows may still need to establish and integrate their individual capital partners. 4. Amount Amount provides digital lending infrastructure for banks and financial institutions, with capabilities spanning loan origination, underwriting, fraud prevention, and account opening. Its platform is designed around helping financial institutions digitize lending products and automate more of the credit lifecycle. Best for: Banks and financial institutions modernizing digital lending and origination. Key capabilities: Digital loan origination Automated underwriting Credit decisioning Fraud prevention Borrower onboarding Banking infrastructure Amount is most relevant when the goal is building or modernizing a digital lending program. For companies whose central requirement is dynamically routing applications among a broad external lender network, a purpose-built multi-lender orchestration layer may be a closer fit. 5. Ocrolus Ocrolus approaches underwriting from the borrower-data side of the stack. Its technology converts financial documents and other borrower information into structured data that lenders can use during underwriting. The platform has a strong focus on document analysis, verification, and lending-specific AI workflows. Best for: Lending teams where document processing and borrower data analysis are major underwriting bottlenecks. Key capabilities: Financial document analysis Data extraction Income and cash-flow analysis Document verification Fraud detection Lending-focused AI workflows Ocrolus can be an important component of an orchestration stack, but it solves a different layer of the problem. A lender or fintech may use Ocrolus to generate underwriting data and then pass that information into a separate decisioning and multi-lender routing platform. How the Top Providers Compare ProviderPrimary StrengthBuilt-In Lender NetworkDecisioningData OrchestrationBest Fit Lendflow End-to-end multi-lender orchestrationYesYesYesEmbedded lending, brokers, marketplaces, fintechs Taktile Flexible credit decisioningNoYesYesFintechs and risk teams Provenir Enterprise decisioning and dataNoYesYesLarge lenders and financial institutions Amount Digital lending infrastructureNoYesYesBanks and financial institutions Ocrolus Underwriting data and document analysisNoSupports decision workflowsYesDocument-heavy lending workflows The most important distinction is between decision orchestration and lender orchestration . A decision engine helps determine whether an applicant satisfies a particular credit policy. Multi-lender orchestration goes one step further by determining which lender or lenders should receive that application and coordinating what happens next. What to Look for in a Multi-Lender Underwriting Orchestration Platform Comparing platforms feature by feature can be misleading because the category covers several different layers of lending infrastructure. Focus on how the platform handles the full application journey instead. Lender Network Breadth If you don't already have capital partners, determine whether the provider offers actual lender connectivity or simply gives you technology for integrating lenders yourself. Network breadth also matters. Different lenders specialize in different industries, borrower profiles, loan sizes, and financing products. More lender coverage creates more opportunities to find an appropriate destination for each qualified borrower. Configurable Routing Logic Routing shouldn't amount to sending every application everywhere. A modern orchestration platform should let you define which lenders receive an application based on eligibility criteria, borrower characteristics, product requirements, and lender preferences. The goal is to route each deal intelligently rather than generate unnecessary submissions. Data Aggregation Underwriting is only as useful as the information feeding it. Look for integrations across bank data, credit bureaus, accounting platforms, identity providers, fraud tools, and business data sources. A unified data layer reduces the need to maintain individual integrations and gives decision models standardized inputs. Decisioning Flexibility Credit policies change. Teams should be able to modify thresholds, lender eligibility requirements, routing priorities, and underwriting rules without rebuilding the entire workflow. Testing and version control become especially important as the number of lenders and policies increases. Document Automation Bank statements, tax returns, IDs, financial statements, and other documents can create a manual bottleneck even when routing is automated. Document extraction and verification should feed structured information directly into underwriting workflows rather than forcing operations teams to re-key borrower data. Unified Borrower Experience The complexity of a multi-lender system should stay behind the scenes. Borrowers should ideally complete one application, upload documents once, and receive relevant offers through a consistent interface regardless of how many lenders participate in the process. Reporting and Analytics Orchestration creates a valuable dataset of its own. Teams should be able to analyze approval rates, lender performance, conversion, routing outcomes, application volume, and funding performance to understand where deals are being won or lost. Decision Engines vs Multi-Lender Orchestration Platforms The terms are sometimes used interchangeably, but they solve different problems. A decision engine answers: Does this borrower satisfy this underwriting policy? A multi-lender orchestration platform answers: Which underwriting policies apply, which lenders are appropriate, where should this application go, and what should happen after each lender responds? That distinction becomes increasingly important as a lending program grows. A company with one lender and one credit policy may only need a decision engine. A marketplace or embedded lending platform working with many capital providers needs another layer to coordinate those decisions and relationships. In practice, sophisticated lending infrastructure often combines both. When Should You Use Multi-Lender Underwriting Orchestration? Multi-lender orchestration becomes valuable when adding lenders creates operational complexity rather than simply increasing distribution. Common signals include: Your team manually determines which lender should receive each application Applications are submitted separately to multiple lender portals Borrowers have to provide the same information more than once Each new lender requires a custom engineering integration Declined applications aren't automatically rerouted Credit policies are maintained across spreadsheets or internal tools Operations teams spend significant time checking lender statuses You can't easily compare approval or conversion rates across lenders These problems become more expensive as application volume and lender count increase. Orchestration turns those individual processes into infrastructure that can be reused across the entire lender network. Build Multi-Lender Underwriting Workflows With Lendflow The best multi-lender underwriting architecture connects three things: data, decisions, and capital . Lendflow brings those layers together through Lendflow Intelligence for borrower data and decisioning, Lendflow Automate for workflow execution, and Lendflow Connect for multi-lender distribution. Instead of maintaining separate integrations and workflows for every capital provider, businesses can connect to a network of 75+ lenders through one infrastructure layer and automatically route applications based on borrower and lender criteria. For teams evaluating providers, the deciding question is simple: Do you need software that helps make an underwriting decision, or infrastructure that can coordinate underwriting across an entire lender ecosystem? If the goal is the latter, look for a platform built around lender connectivity, configurable routing, unified borrower data, and workflow automation—not just a standalone credit decision engine. ‍

title: JONAS BROTHERS BRING THE BURNING UP TOUR ALL OVER AGAIN TO MGM GRAND GARDEN ARENA NOVEMBER 28, 2026
How Auraciel Medihealth Made More Time for People, as Its Clinic Network Grew
summary: Learn how Neoasia Group built scalable HR systems to streamline hiring, improve performance, and support sustainable growth.
body_text: Meet Auraciel Medihealth Every clinic visit depends on more than what happens in the consultation room. Behind patient care are the people, schedules, records, and everyday processes that keep each location running. Based in Penang, Auraciel Medihealth provides occupational healthcare and primary care services across a growing network of clinics. As the organisation expands, its aim is to become more technology-driven while maintaining high standards of patient care. That ambition also shapes how Auraciel thinks about its 100 employees. “We believe our employees are our greatest asset.” Auraciel wants to build a workplace where employees feel supported, valued, and able to grow professionally. For the team, that means having clear HR processes, fair policies, continuous learning opportunities, and digital tools that reduce administrative work rather than add to it. Employees can then spend more of their time delivering quality healthcare.

title: Tecogen Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
body_text: Tecogen Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Download as PDF August 12, 2026 Related Documents Audio Earnings Webcast NORTH BILLERICA, MA / ACCESS Newswire / August 12, 2026 / Tecogen Inc. (NYSE American:TGEN), a leading manufacturer of clean energy products, reported revenues of $5.75 million and net loss of $2.15 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to revenues of $7.29 million, and a net loss of $1.46 million in 2025. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, revenues were $12.08 million, and the net loss was $4.27 million, compared to revenues of $14.57 million, and a net loss of $2.12 million in 2025. Our cash and cash equivalents balance was $6.78 million at June 30, 2026. Abinand Rangesh, CEO of Tecogen, commented, "Over the last two months, we have been flat out hosting product demonstrations. Reaching this point has taken many grueling months of relationship building, but we may now have a shot at the hyperscalers and big brand data centers. We hosted 12 product demonstrations in total, six in person, and six virtual. Cumulatively, these data centers represent greater than eight gigawatts of capacity operating today and many gigawatts of contracted development. To put this in perspective, these data centers control 15% to 20% of all US data center capacity. Unlike previously, when our opportunity pipeline was primarily filled with smaller data centers, most of the data centers that attended the recent demos have the capital, permitted projects, and the influence to shape the whole industry. My confidence level in our prospects has increased to the point that we are building inventory of our dual power source chiller and power generation systems in order to respond quickly as these opportunities progress. Our non-data center backlog currently stands at approximately $8 million with $2 million or more in additional orders expected over the next few months. Therefore, we expect our Q3 product revenue to be higher than Q1 and Q2, and our service revenue is currently 10% higher compared to the same period last year. We finished the quarter with over $6.78 million in cash and our cash position today remains over $6 million due to lower cash burn because of cost reductions and deposit collection. Tomorrow, I will be able to shed more light on why it has taken this long and why I think our prospects are fundamentally different now." Key Takeaways Net Loss and Earnings Per Share The net loss for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $2.15 million compared to a net loss of $1.46 million for the same period of 2025, an increase in the net loss of $0.68 million, due to decreased gross profit from our Products segment and an increase in operating expenses. EPS for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 was a loss of $(0.07)/share and $(0.06), respectively. The net loss for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $4.27 million compared to a net loss of $2.12 million for the same period of 2025, an increase in the net loss of $2.15 million, due to decreased gross profit from our Products segment and an increase in operating expenses. EPS for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 was a loss of $(0.14)/share and $(0.08)/share, respectively. Loss from Operations Loss from operations for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $2.15 million compared to a loss from operations of $1.41 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $0.74 million, due to decreased gross profit from our Products segment and an increase in operating expenses. Loss from operations for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $4.29 million compared to a loss from operations of $2.01 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $2.28 million, due to decreased gross profit from our Products segment and an increase in operating expenses. Revenues Revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $5.75 million compared to $7.29 million for the same period in 2025, a 21.2% decrease. Products revenues in the quarter ended June 30, 2026 were $1.13 million compared to $3.16 million for the same period in 2025, a decrease of 64.0%. The decrease in revenue during the quarter ended June 30, 2026 is due to decreased chiller and cogeneration revenue. Services revenues in the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $4.38 million, compared to $3.97 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of 10.3% due to increased revenues from the acquired Aegis maintenance contracts and increased revenues from existing service contracts. Energy Production revenues in the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $0.24 million compared to $0.17 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of 35.4%. The increase in Energy Production revenue is due to improved site operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026. Revenues for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $12.08 million compared to $14.57 million for the same period in 2025, a 17.1% decrease. Products revenues in the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $2.31 million compared to $5.69 million for the same period in 2025, a decrease of 59.4%. The decrease in revenue during the six months ended June 30, 2026 is due to decreased chiller and cogeneration revenue. Services revenues in the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $9.01 million, compared to $8.21 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of 9.8% due to increased revenues from existing contracts and increased revenues from the acquired Aegis maintenance contracts. Energy Production revenues in the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $0.76 million compared to $0.67 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of 12.9%. The increase in Energy Production revenue is due to improved site operations in the six months ended June 30, 2026. Gross Profit Gross profit for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $2.17 million compared to $2.46 million in the same period in 2025. Gross margin increased to 37.8% in the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to 33.8% for the same period in 2025. The increase is due to higher Products segment margin in the three months ended June 30, 2026. Gross profit for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $4.76 million compared to $5.68 million in the same period in 2025. Gross margin increased to 39.4% in the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to 39.0% for the same period in 2025. The increase in gross margin was due to higher Products segment margin in the six months ended June 30, 2026. Operating Expenses Operating expenses increased $0.45 million, or 11.6%, to $4.32 million in the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to $3.87 million in the same period in 2025, due to increased payroll, benefits, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation and business insurance. Operating expenses increased $1.36 million, or 17.7%, to $9.05 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to $7.69 million in the same period in 2025, due to increased payroll, benefits, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation and business insurance. Adjusted EBITDA Adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.68 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to negative $1.16 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, adjusted EBITDA was a negative $3.36 million compared to a negative $1.54 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. (Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income or loss attributable to Tecogen, adjusted for interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation expense, unrealized gain or loss on investment securities, goodwill impairment charges and other non-cash non-recurring charges or gains including abandonment of intangible assets and asset impairment. See the table following the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations for a reconciliation from net income (loss) to Adjusted EBITDA, as well as important disclosures about the Company's use of Adjusted EBITDA). title: RFK Jr Urges Parents to Vaccinate Children Against Measles as US Cases Reach a 35 Year High

body_text: The United States is experiencing one of its largest measles outbreaks in decades, prompting an unexpected public statement from Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Despite being widely known for years of skepticism toward vaccines, Kennedy has now publicly encouraged parents to ensure their children receive the measles vaccine before returning to school. His comments have drawn national attention because they appear to mark a significant departure from his previous public messaging on vaccines. At the same time, the statement comes as measles infections continue to rise across the country, raising concerns among public health officials about the future of disease prevention in the United States. Measles Cases Continue to Rise Across America According to the latest public health data, the United States has recorded more than 2,300 confirmed measles cases in 2026. This surpasses the total number reported during the previous year and represents the highest annual case count seen in approximately 35 years. Health experts warn that the increase is particularly concerning because measles was officially declared eliminated in the United States in 2000. While imported cases have occurred periodically, widespread outbreaks have remained relatively uncommon until recent years. The growing number of infections has renewed concerns that the country could lose its measles elimination status if transmission continues to spread. RFK Jr Calls for Childhood Measles Vaccination During an interview on CNN's State of the Union , Robert F. Kennedy Jr. addressed parents directly regarding measles prevention. He stated that parents should vaccinate their children against measles and acknowledged that the vaccine is highly effective. Kennedy also referenced the Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) vaccine, encouraging families to receive the combined immunization that has long been recommended by health authorities. The remarks surprised many observers because Kennedy has spent years questioning vaccine safety and effectiveness. Before joining the federal government, he became one of the most recognizable voices within the vaccine skepticism movement, often promoting claims that were rejected by scientific research. A Major Shift From Previous Vaccine Messaging Kennedy's latest comments stand in sharp contrast to his previous public positions. For years, he questioned vaccine safety, criticized immunization programs, and repeatedly raised concerns about childhood vaccines. Many public health organizations argued that his statements contributed to increased vaccine hesitancy among parents. Even after becoming the nation's top health official, Kennedy often described vaccination as a personal decision rather than strongly encouraging routine immunization. Because of this history, many medical experts view his latest endorsement of the measles vaccine as a notable shift in messaging, although questions remain about whether it represents a broader change in his views. Public Health Experts Welcome the Recommendation Many health professionals welcomed Kennedy's statement encouraging measles vaccination, regardless of his previous record. The MMR vaccine has consistently been shown to provide strong protection against measles. According to health authorities, two doses offer approximately 97 percent effectiveness in preventing infection. Medical experts continue to stress that widespread vaccination remains the most effective way to prevent outbreaks and protect vulnerable populations, including infants, individuals with weakened immune systems, and those who cannot receive vaccines for medical reasons. Public health officials also emphasize that maintaining high vaccination rates helps create community immunity, reducing opportunities for the virus to spread. Critics Say the Message Came Too Late Although Kennedy's recommendation was welcomed by some experts, others argued that it arrived after months of rapidly increasing infections. Throughout the outbreak, critics accused the administration of failing to aggressively promote vaccination campaigns. Some believe stronger messaging earlier in the year could have encouraged more families to vaccinate their children before outbreaks expanded across multiple communities. Health officials continue monitoring dozens of active outbreaks nationwide while urging eligible individuals to receive recommended vaccinations. Heated Television Interview Draws Attention The interview itself also became a major news story. CNN anchor Dana Bash repeatedly questioned Kennedy about vaccine safety and his responsibility for increasing vaccine hesitancy. During the exchange, Kennedy denied any responsibility for the nationwide rise in measles cases. Instead, he suggested that vaccine refusal within certain religious communities and broader international health conditions contributed to the outbreaks. The conversation became increasingly tense as Kennedy criticized Bash's questions and challenged several of her statements. Bash responded by expressing frustration that misinformation surrounding vaccines continues to influence public opinion while preventable diseases are spreading. The exchange quickly generated widespread discussion across television, social media, and political commentary. Additional Health Claims Spark Controversy Beyond discussing measles, Kennedy also made several claims involving other public health issues. During the interview, he questioned aspects of COVID-19 vaccination policy and repeated controversial statements regarding conditions such as Lyme disease, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and autism. Many scientists and medical organizations have stated that these claims are not supported by established scientific evidence. Researchers continue to emphasize that decades of peer reviewed studies support the safety and effectiveness of recommended childhood vaccines. Public health experts caution that inaccurate medical information can reduce public confidence and make disease prevention more difficult. Why Vaccination Remains Important Measles is among the most contagious infectious diseases known. The virus spreads easily through coughing, sneezing, and airborne particles that can remain in indoor environments for extended periods. Individuals who are not vaccinated face a much higher risk of infection during outbreaks. Complications can include pneumonia, brain inflammation, hospitalization, permanent disability, and in rare cases, death. Routine vaccination has dramatically reduced measles cases worldwide and remains one of the most successful public health interventions ever developed. Health authorities continue recommending that eligible children receive the full MMR vaccination schedule according to established immunization guidelines. Looking Ahead The coming months will likely determine whether the United States can control the current outbreak before schools fully reopen nationwide. Kennedy's endorsement of measles vaccination may encourage some hesitant parents to reconsider immunization. However, many experts argue that sustained public education, transparent communication, and strong support from healthcare professionals will be necessary to restore confidence and reduce future outbreaks. As measles cases continue to climb, public health officials remain focused on increasing vaccination coverage and preventing additional community transmission. Disclaimer This article is a written summary created for informational and educational purposes. It is not intended to replace professional medical advice or official public health guidance. Readers should consult qualified healthcare providers and trusted public health organizations for the latest recommendations regarding vaccinations and infectious diseases. Source: The Guardian , August 2, 2026.

title: How Do You Store Camping Gear?
summary: Packing for a camping trip is easier when your gear is already organized and ready to go. body_text: Packing for a camping trip is easier when your gear is already organized and ready to go. The best way to store camping gear is to clean and dry everything after each trip, organize equipment by category, and keep frequently used items together in labeled bins or other easy-to-access storage. Tents, sleeping bags, coolers, camp chairs, cooking equipment, and outdoor gear can take up a lot of room at home. Creating a consistent storage system can help you save space, find what you need, and spend less time packing before your next trip. How Should You Organize Camping Gear at Home? Organize camping gear by function so related items are stored together. This makes packing faster and helps you see what needs to be cleaned, repaired, replaced, or restocked before your next trip. Consider creating categories such as: Shelter: Tents, stakes, guylines and tarps Sleeping: Sleeping bags, sleeping pads and camping pillows Camp kitchen: Stoves, cookware, utensils and other cooking supplies Lighting and essentials: Lanterns, flashlights, first-aid kits and tools Outdoor activities: Backpacks, fishing equipment and other recreational gear Camp furniture: Folding chairs and tables Family supplies: Kids’ or pet-specific camping gear Store smaller items in labeled bins or containers so you can quickly find and pack an entire category. How Can You Store Camping Gear in a Small Space? To store camping gear in a small home or apartment, take advantage of vertical and underused spaces. Shelving units, stackable bins, over-the-door organizers, wall-mounted storage, and under-bed containers can provide additional room without taking over your everyday living areas. Keep frequently used equipment somewhere easy to reach, while seasonal or bulky gear can go in less accessible storage areas. If tents, coolers, folding chairs, outdoor equipment, and other bulky items are taking up too much room at home, a self-storage unit can provide additional space between trips. How Do You Keep Camping Gear Ready for the Next Trip? Keep camping gear ready for your next trip by cleaning, drying, restocking, and reorganizing it as soon as you return home. Once everything is ready for storage, return it to the same designated bins, shelves, or containers. You don’t necessarily need to unpack every camping bin after each trip. If items are clean, dry, and don’t need to be replenished, keeping your basic camping setup together can make it easier to grab what you need next time. A digital camping checklist can also help you track consumable or trip-specific items, such as food, toiletries, clothing, and other supplies that shouldn’t remain packed between trips. How Should You Store Tents and Sleeping Bags? Tents and sleeping bags should be completely clean and dry before being stored. Packing damp outdoor gear can encourage mildew, odors, and material deterioration. After a trip, unpack your tent and allow it to air-dry completely before putting it away. Sleeping bags should also be thoroughly dry before storage. Follow the manufacturer’s storage instructions for your specific tent or sleeping bag, since recommendations can vary by material and design. How Should You Prepare Camping Gear for Storage? Clean and inspect camping equipment before putting it away so it is ready for your next trip. Before storing your gear: Air-dry tents, tarps and sleeping gear completely. Clean cookware, dishes and utensils. Empty and clean coolers. Remove food and other perishable items. Check flashlights, lanterns and other equipment. Remove batteries from devices before longer-term storage when appropriate. Restock first-aid kits and other supplies. Keep small accessories together in labeled pouches or bins. Taking care of these tasks immediately after a trip can help prevent unpleasant surprises the next time you go camping. Can You Store Camping Gear in a Storage Unit? A storage unit can be useful for bulky or seasonal camping and outdoor equipment that you don’t have room to keep at home. Depending on what you own, that might include extra tents, coolers, folding tables and chairs, hiking packs, fishing equipment, or other outdoor gear. Keeping less frequently used equipment in a storage unit can free up closets, garages, and other areas of your home while giving your camping gear a dedicated place between trips. Before storing any camping equipment, make sure it is clean and completely dry and check any applicable storage restrictions for items such as fuel, propane, or other potentially hazardous materials. How Can You Make Packing for Camping Faster? A consistent storage system can make packing for camping faster because you don’t have to reorganize your gear before every trip. Keep a master camping checklist, restock supplies when you return home, store equipment by category, and use labeled grab-and-go bins for items you regularly bring with you. Before each trip, you can focus on adding food, clothing, and destination-specific supplies instead of rebuilding your camping setup from scratch. If camping and outdoor gear is taking over your closets, garage, or spare room, Public Storage can give you additional space for belongings you don’t need at home every day. Find self-storage near you and compare available unit sizes and features. When your camping gear is organized between trips, you can spend less time searching, sorting, and packing—and more time getting outside.

title: BioMarin Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial and Operating Results
body_text: Second Quarter 2026 Total Revenues Increased 20% Year-over-year to $990 million Stronger Growth Expectations Drive Increased Guidance for Full-year 2026 Total Revenues, VOXZOGO®, and Non-GAAP Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) Addition of GALAFOLD® and POMBILITI® + OPFOLDA®, with Cost Synergies, Expected to Accelerate Revenue Growth, Non-GAAP Diluted EPS Accretion, Non-GAAP Operating Margin Expansion, and Operating Cash Flow through the Mid-2030s Conference Call and Webcast Scheduled Today at 4:30 p.m. ET SAN RAFAEL, Calif. , Aug. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc. (NASDAQ: BMRN) today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. "This quarter, we executed strongly across our portfolio while rapidly integrating Amicus into BioMarin's operations and advancing plans to accelerate growth for GALAFOLD and POMBILITI + OPFOLDA, and extending the benefit of these medicines to more patients worldwide," said Alexander Hardy, President and Chief Executive Officer of BioMarin. "Strong global demand led us to increase full-year VOXZOGO revenue guidance to at least $1 billion in 2026. Adding to this momentum is the opportunity to advance our second potential indication with VOXZOGO, hypochondroplasia, based on recent pivotal data that exceeded our expectations." Mr. Hardy added, "With our larger, more diversified commercial portfolio of innovative medicines, we are positioned to deliver additional growth and increased profitability. We expect strong execution through the remainder of 2026, bringing together our expanded portfolio, scale and disciplined integration efforts to reach more patients living with serious genetic conditions around the world." 2026 Business and Pipeline Highlights Innovation BioMarin recently submitted its supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the approval of VOXZOGO for the treatment of hypochondroplasia. If approved, VOXZOGO would be the first targeted therapy for the treatment of hypochondroplasia, with a potential 2027 launch. The company plans to provide an update on the application status as part of its third quarter earnings update. In May, the company announced that the Phase 3 CANOPY-HCH-3 study of VOXZOGO in children with hypochondroplasia met its primary endpoint, with a statistically significant increase in annualized growth velocity (AGV) at week 52 versus placebo (LS mean difference +2.33 cm/yr, p<0.0001), along with significant improvements in standing height, height Z-score, and the key secondary endpoint of arm span. The full Phase 3 dataset will be shared in a late-breaking oral presentation at the European Society for Paediatric Endocrinology Annual Meeting in September. In June, at the Endocrine Society Annual Meeting (ENDO 2026), a Phase 2 investigator-sponsored three-year extension study of VOXZOGO in 13 children with hypochondroplasia showed sustained improvements in growth with a favorable safety profile. Mean AGV increased from 4.27 cm/year at baseline to 7.24 cm/year at year one (p<0.001) and remained above baseline through year three, with mean height standard deviation score (SDS) improving 0.72 over the three years. Also at ENDO 2026, the company presented Phase 1 data for BMN 333, BioMarin's long-acting C-type natriuretic peptide (CNP) for achondroplasia. In a single-ascending-dose study in healthy adults, BMN 333 demonstrated sustained exposure supporting weekly dosing and was well tolerated, with free CNP exposure at the highest dose more than 13-fold that of another long-acting CNP agent, reflecting its potential to become a new standard of care in achondroplasia. The Phase 2/3 study is enrolling, with a data update expected in 2027. In July, BioMarin announced that the FDA accepted its sNDA for full approval of VOXZOGO in children with achondroplasia, with a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of February 28, 2027. In the second quarter, the European Commission approved PALYNZIQ® for adolescents 12 years and older with phenylketonuria (PKU). PALYNZIQ is the only therapy that enables people with PKU to reach physiologic Phe levels while reducing dietary restrictions, regardless of severity. During the quarter, BioMarin added BMN 820 (formerly DMX-200) to its portfolio, a first-in-class oral CCR2 inhibitor for focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) for which BioMarin holds exclusive U.S. commercialization rights. BMN 820 has the potential to treat a broad FSGS population, regardless of nephrotic syndrome status, and represents a U.S. total addressable patient population of approximately 30,000. The Phase 3 ACTION 3 trial is ongoing, with pivotal data expected in 2028. BMN 351, BioMarin's Phase 1/2 candidate for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, continued in development. The company expects to provide a program update by year-end. Following the pivotal ENERGY 3 trial results, previously announced in May, in which BMN 401 did not meet one of its two co-primary endpoints for the treatment of ENPP1 deficiency, BioMarin has now made the decision to discontinue development of BMN 401 across all indications. In July, BioMarin and the n-Lorem Foundation entered a collaboration and global exclusive license agreement to develop a first-in-disease antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) medicine for ReNU syndrome, a serious, rare neurodevelopmental condition with no approved targeted therapies. ReNU syndrome has an expected global population of approximately 100,000. Growth BioMarin expects peak revenue for GALAFOLD to be approximately $1.4 billion by the mid-2030s and for POMBILITI + OPFOLDA to be approximately $1.2 billion by the mid-to-late-2030s. BioMarin expects these high growth therapies to benefit from its global scale and proven commercial capabilities. Metabolic Conditions (formerly Enzyme Therapies) revenue grew 25% Y/Y in the second quarter of 2026, driven by the additions of GALAFOLD and POMBILITI + OPFOLDA and continued strength from PALYNZIQ. The number of patients on therapy grew across all BioMarin-marketed therapies, both Y/Y and sequentially. Strong U.S. and global demand led to increased full-year 2026 VOXZOGO revenue guidance to a low end of $1 billion. The number of children being treated with VOXZOGO globally increased by more than 20% Y/Y in the second quarter. In the U.S., the majority of new patient starts were under two years of age, and the region drove approximately 25% of total VOXZOGO revenue during the quarter. Value Commitment As part of the acquisition of Amicus, which closed on April 27, 2026, the company identified approximately $280 million of cost reductions on a GAAP basis, and approximately $220 million of cost reductions on a Non-GAAP basis, expected to be fully realized in 2028, representing an approximately 50% reduction from Amicus-reported 2025 GAAP and Non-GAAP operating expenses, respectively. Synergies reflect a reduction of Amicus' legacy labor costs and external spend and are expected to be largely driven by general and administrative functions, with the large majority of sales and marketing capabilities retained to support continued commercial growth. GALAFOLD and POMBILITI + OPFOLDA, combined, are expected to reach over 60% Non-GAAP Operating Margin by 2030. The company is targeting gross leverage below 2.5 times by mid-year 2027, an acceleration by approximately one year of prior timeline guidance provided at deal announcement, supported by profitability growth of the combined company. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights Total Revenues for the second quarter of 2026 were $990 million, an increase of $165 million compared to the same period in 2025, primarily driven by revenues from GALAFOLD and POMBILITI + OPFOLDA, which were acquired from Amicus on April 27, 2026, as well as new patients initiating VOXZOGO therapy across all regions and growth in U.S. patients treated with PALYNZIQ. These increases were partially offset by lower VIMIZIM® revenue due to the timing of large government orders outside the U.S. and lower ALDURAZYME® sales volume due to the timing of order fulfillment to Sanofi. GAAP Net Income for the second quarter of 2026 decreased to $45 million compared to $241 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by the acquisition of Amicus, including integration and restructuring costs, intangible asset amortization, interest expense from debt issued to finance a portion of the transaction, and amortization of inventory fair value step-up. Other drivers included higher sales and marketing spend to support newly acquired products and global expansion of VOXZOGO and higher Research and Development (R&D) spend related to BMN 401, which was acquired in the third quarter of 2025, partially offset by higher gross profit driven by revenue growth as described above. Non-GAAP Income for the second quarter of 2026 decreased to $236 million compared to $282 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by higher interest expense, higher sales and marketing spend to support newly acquired products and global expansion of VOXZOGO, and higher R&D spend related to BMN 401, partially offset by higher gross profit driven by revenue growth as described above. summary: MACAU, Aug. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Melco Resorts & Entertainment Limited (Nasdaq: MLCO), a developer, owner and operator of integrated resort facilities in Asia and Europe, today announces that it will release its unaudited financial results for the second quarter of 2026 on Thursday, August
body_text: MACAU, Aug. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Melco Resorts & Entertainment Limited (Nasdaq: MLCO), a developer, owner and operator of integrated resort facilities in Asia and Europe, today announces that it will release its unaudited financial results for the second quarter of 2026 on Thursday, August 13, 2026 to be followed by a conference call on the same day at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time (or 8:30 p.m. Singapore Time). To join the conference call, please register in advance using the below Online Registration Link. Upon registering, each participant will receive the dial-in numbers, passcode and a unique Personal PIN which can be used to join the conference. Online Registration Link: https://s1.c-conf.com/diamondpass/10055249-7qhfkc.html An audio webcast and replay of the conference call will also be available at http://www.melco-resorts.com . These statements are made under the “safe harbor” provisions of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Melco Resorts & Entertainment Limited (the “Company”) may also make forward-looking statements in its periodic reports to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”), in its annual report to shareholders, in press releases and other written materials and in oral statements made by its officers, directors or employees to third parties. Statements that are not historical facts, including statements about the Company’s beliefs and expectations, are forward-looking statements. These factors include, but are not limited to, (i) changes in the gaming market and visitations in Macau, the Philippines, the Republic of Cyprus and Sri Lanka, (ii) local and global economic conditions, (iii) capital and credit market volatility, (iv) our anticipated growth strategies, (v) risks associated with the implementation of the amended Macau gaming law by the Macau government, (vi) gaming authority and other governmental approvals and regulations, and (vii) our future business development, results of operations and financial condition. In some cases, forward-looking statements can be identified by words or phrases such as “may,” “will,” “expect,” “anticipate,” “target,” “aim,” “estimate,” “intend,” “plan,” “believe,” “potential,” “continue,” “is/are likely to” or other similar expressions. All information provided in this press release is as of the date of this press release, and the Company undertakes no duty to update such information, except as required under applicable law. About Melco Resorts & Entertainment Limited The Company, with its American depositary shares listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (Nasdaq: MLCO), is a developer, owner and operator of integrated resort facilities in Asia and Europe. The Company currently operates City of Dreams ( www.cityofdreamsmacau.com ) and Altira Macau ( www.altiramacau.com ), integrated resorts located in Cotai and Taipa, Macau, respectively. Its business also includes the Mocha Clubs ( www.mochaclubs.com ), the only non-casino based operation of electronic gaming machines in Macau. In addition, the Company operates Studio City ( www.studiocity-macau.com ), a cinematically-themed integrated resort in Cotai, Macau. In the Philippines, the Company operates and manages City of Dreams Manila ( www.cityofdreamsmanila.com ), an integrated resort in the Entertainment City complex in Manila. In Europe, the Company operates City of Dreams Mediterranean, an integrated resort in Limassol, in the Republic of Cyprus ( www.cityofdreamsmed.com.cy ) and licensed satellite casinos in other cities in Cyprus (the “Cyprus Casinos”). In South Asia, the Company operates the casino and manages the Nüwa hotel at City of Dreams Sri Lanka ( www.cityofdreamssrilanka.com ), an integrated resort in Colombo, Sri Lanka. title: Parsons Awarded First Task Order Under DTRA CTRIC IV to Support Chemical Threat Reduction Efforts in Southeast Asia

The program supports U.S. Pacific Command (USPACOM) priorities by strengthening regional
body_text: Parsons Awarded First Task Order Under DTRA CTRIC IV to Support Chemical Threat Reduction Efforts in Southeast Asia 08/13/2026 PDF Version Key Takeaways: Parsons secured the first task order issued under DTRA’s CTRIC IV contract, reinforcing the company’s position as a trusted partner in delivering integrated threat reduction solutions worldwide. The program supports U.S. Pacific Command (USPACOM) priorities by strengthening regional chemical threat monitoring and response capabilities. Parsons will deliver training, exercises, and workshops to enhance partner nation capabilities across Southeast Asia, including Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines. CHANTILLY, Va., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Parsons Corporation (NYSE: PSN) announced today it has secured the first task order under the Defense Threat Reduction Agency’s (DTRA) Cooperative Threat Reduction Integration Contract (CTRIC) IV, marking an early milestone on the contract vehicle and reinforcing the company’s leadership in countering weapons of mass destruction. Under the task order, Parsons will support DTRA’s Global Threat Reduction directorate by designing and delivering chemical security training across Southeast Asia. The effort will strengthen partner nation capabilities in countries such as Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines through training courses, exercises, and workshops that enhance preparedness, detection, and response to chemical threats. “This award reflects our long-standing partnership with DTRA and commitment to advancing global threat reduction programs,” said Martin Boson, president of Engineered Systems for Parsons. “By delivering scalable solutions, training, and mission support, we are helping allied nations strengthen detection, response, and mitigation capabilities while supporting broader security objectives in Southeast Asia.” The program supports USPACOM priorities by enhancing partner-nation capacity to monitor and secure chemical materials of concern, helping reduce risk and improve collective security outcomes. The award represents a significant milestone for Parsons as the first task order issued under the CTRIC IV contract, reinforcing the company’s position as a trusted partner in delivering integrated threat reduction solutions worldwide. Parsons brings decades of experience supporting DTRA, and this award further positions the company to continue supporting the Global Threat Reduction Directorate in addressing evolving weapons of mass destruction threats worldwide. To learn more about Parsons’ global security and mission solutions, visit parsons.com/security-and-mission-solutions/ . title: How Toma handles your data under GDPR
summary: Toma is built to comply with GDPR. Here's how we handle the data dealerships trust us with, and how to get it deleted.
body_text: ← Blog How Toma handles your data under GDPR Toma is built to comply with GDPR. Here's how we handle the data dealerships trust us with, and how to get it deleted. By Anthony · April 2026 When a dealership uses Toma, we process personal data on its behalf: a caller's name, their phone number, what they asked for, and the recording of the call. The EU's General Data Protection Regulation sets the rules for handling that kind of data, and Toma is built to follow them. Most of our customers are US dealerships. The principles behind GDPR are good practice anywhere: collect less, protect what you hold, and let people control their own data. We apply them across the board. What GDPR asks of us Two ideas sit at its core. Collect only the data you need for a clear purpose. Give people real control over the data you hold, including the right to see it, correct it, and have it deleted. Both shape how Toma is built. How it works at Toma We collect the minimum. Toma takes only what the job needs: contact details, appointment information from your dealer management system, and call recordings and transcripts. Nothing more. One contract, one processor. You sign a Master Service Agreement and a Data Processing Addendum with Toma, and that's it. We act as the single processor of record. The AI vendors behind Toma are bound by our terms, including a ban on keeping or training on your data, so you never have to manage them yourself. We keep it only as long as needed. Customer data lives for the length of our relationship. If an account closes, we hold the data for 30 days in case you come back, then delete it, unless the law requires us to keep it longer. It's protected the whole time. Data is encrypted at rest and in transit, isolated per customer, and stored on AWS in US data centers. The same controls that earned our ISO 27001 certificate and SOC 2 Type 2 report apply here. Your data, your rights If someone whose data we process wants to see it or have it removed, we honor that. Email support@toma.com and we delete everything we have no legal reason to keep, within 30 days. Get our DPA Our Data Processing Addendum and security reports are available through our trust center at trust.toma.com . Your privacy and procurement teams can review them before you sign.

title: Hampton by Hilton Introduces Its First Guest-Created Waffle Flavor
summary: Winning recipe arrives at Hampton by Hilton as new research finds travelers don’t waffle on their love for hotel breakfast
body_text: Listen to this article 0:00 Winning recipe arrives at Hampton by Hilton as new research finds travelers don’t waffle on their love for hotel breakfast Beginning this month, guests can enjoy Hampton by Hilton’s first-ever guest-created waffle, a limited-time Peach Cobbler flavor available at nearly 2,500 participating hotels across the United States and Canada. New Hampton by Hilton research conducted with Wired Research found 42% of travelers say a great hotel breakfast makes them happy before hitting the road, while nearly four in 10 (39%) say a hot breakfast they did not have to make feels as rewarding as a spa day. The Peach Cobbler Waffle was created by Hampton’s first Guest Waffle Boss, Kaylee Voight of East Lansing, Michigan, and joins a breakfast tradition that inspires guests to make an estimated 30 million waffles at Hampton hotels each year. MCLEAN, Va. – Fresh off the waffle iron: Hampton by Hilton’s Peach Cobbler Waffle, the brand's first-ever guest-created waffle flavor, is rolling out this month at nearly 2,500 participating hotels across the U.S. and Canada. As the winning recipe in Hampton's inaugural Guest Waffle Boss competition , this limited-time creation stacks ripe peaches, oat crumble, caramel sauce and whipped cream on top of Hampton's beloved guest-baked Belgian waffle. Just in time for National Waffle Day on Aug. 24, it's giving travelers one more reason to get out of bed for breakfast. Breakfast has long been known as the most important meal of the day, but according to travelers, it might just be the happiest, too. According to a new Hampton by Hilton study conducted with Wired Research: 42% of travelers say a great hotel breakfast makes them happy before hitting the road. Two-thirds (66%) are more likely to enjoy a sit-down breakfast while traveling than at home. Nearly four in 10 (39%) say a hot breakfast they don't have to cook leaves them just as happy as a spa day. "At Hampton, breakfast has always been about more than what's on the plate, it's a reflection of Hamptonality, the warm, reliable hospitality our guests know and love," said Shruti Gandhi Buckley, senior vice president and brand leader, Hampton by Hilton. "It's rewarding to see travelers tell us what we've long believed: breakfast is one of the moments guests look forward to most during a stay. Every morning, guests gather around our signature waffle station to start the day together, so inviting them to help create our next waffle flavor felt like a natural way to celebrate one of Hampton's most beloved traditions and bring Hamptonality to life in a whole new way." Hampton by Hilton - Peach Cobbler Waffle Today, guests make an estimated 30 million waffles each year at Hampton hotels, enough to fill the biggest stadium in America – Michigan Stadium, in the home state of Hampton’s Guest Waffle Boss – 278 times over. From classic favorites to seasonal flavors like Red Velvet, Pumpkin Spice, S'mores and now Peach Cobbler, Hampton continues to evolve its breakfast tradition, proving that even an iconic guest favorite can keep getting better through thoughtful innovation. Meet Hampton's First Guest Waffle Boss Hampton by Hilton - Guest Waffle Boss Kaylee Making Waffle Every great waffle has a story, and this one starts in East Lansing, Michigan. Last National Waffle Day, Hampton invited breakfast lovers across the country to dream up the brand's next signature waffle flavor through its first-ever Guest Waffle Boss competition. Kaylee Voight's Peach Cobbler creation rose to the top, earning her one million Hilton Honors Points, a five-night stay at any Hampton by Hilton worldwide and, perhaps most importantly, bragging rights as the creator of Hampton's first-ever guest-inspired waffle flavor. Travelers were defined as U.S. adults who traveled domestically for at least one night in the past two years. The margin of error is ±3.1% for the general population and ±2.4% for travelers. Inferred Resource Inferred Mineral Resource is that part of a mineral resource for which quantity and grade or quality are estimated on the basis of limited geological evidence and sampling. The level of geological uncertainty associated with an Inferred Mineral Resource is too high to apply relevant technical and economic factors likely to influence the prospects of economic extraction in a manner useful for evaluation of economic viability. Because an Inferred Mineral Resource has the lowest level of geological confidence of all mineral resources, which prevents the application of the modifying factors in a manner useful for evaluation of economic viability, an Inferred Mineral Resource may not be considered when assessing the economic viability of a mining project, and may not be converted to a mineral reserve. Indicated Resource Indicated Mineral Resource is that part of a mineral resource for which quantity and grade or quality are estimated on the basis of adequate geological evidence and sampling. The level of geological certainty associated with an Indicated Mineral Resource is sufficient to allow a qualified person to apply modifying factors in sufficient detail to support mine planning and evaluation of the economic viability of the deposit. Because an Indicated Mineral Resource has a lower level of confidence than the level of confidence of a Measured Mineral Resource, an Indicated Mineral Resource may only be converted to a Probable Mineral Reserve. Measured Resource Measured Mineral Resource is that part of a mineral resource for which quantity and grade or quality are estimated on the basis of conclusive geological evidence and sampling. The level of geological certainty associated with a Measured Mineral Resource is sufficient to allow a qualified person to apply modifying factors, as defined in this section, in sufficient detail to support detailed mine planning and final evaluation of the economic viability of the deposit. Because a Measured Mineral Resource has a higher level of confidence than the level of confidence of either an Indicated Mineral Resource or an Inferred Mineral Resource, a Measured Mineral Resource may be converted to a Proven Mineral Reserve or to a Probable Mineral Reserve. Mineral Reserve Mineral Reserve is an estimate of tonnage and grade or quality of indicated and measured mineral resources that, in the opinion of the qualified person, can be the basis of an economically viable project. More specifically, it is the economically mineable part of a measured or indicated mineral resource, which includes diluting materials and allowances for losses that may occur when the material is mined or extracted. Probable Mineral Reserve Probable Mineral Reserve is the economically mineable part of an indicated and, in some cases, a measured mineral resource. Proven Mineral Reserve Proven Mineral Reserve is the economically mineable part of a measured mineral resource and can only result from conversion of a measured mineral resource. Initial Assessment An Initial Assessment is a preliminary technical and economic study of the economic potential of all or parts of mineralization to support the disclosure of mineral resources. The Initial Assessment must be prepared by a qualified person and must include appropriate assessments of reasonably assumed technical and economic factors, together with any other relevant operational factors, that are necessary to demonstrate at the time of reporting that there are reasonable prospects for economic extraction. An Initial Assessment is required for disclosure of mineral resources but cannot be used as the basis for disclosure of mineral reserves. An Initial Assessment is preliminary in nature and includes Inferred Mineral Resources that are considered too speculative geologically to have the economic considerations applied that would enable them to be classified as mineral reserves. There is no certainty that the economic results of an initial assessment will be realized. The mineral resource estimates presented in the ABTC Tonopah Flats Initial Assessment were performed by third-party, qualified person RESPEC, LLC and were classified by geological and quantitative confidence in accordance with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Regulation S-K 1300. Pre-Feasibility Study A Preliminary Feasibility Study (or Pre-Feasibility Study) is a comprehensive study of a range of options for the technical and economic viability of a mineral project that has advanced to a stage where a qualified person has determined (in the case of underground mining) a preferred mining method, or (in the case of surface mining) a pit configuration, and in all cases has determined an effective method of mineral processing and an effective plan to sell the product. A Pre-Feasibility Study includes a financial analysis based on reasonable assumptions, based on appropriate testing, about the modifying factors and the evaluation of any other relevant factors that are sufficient for a qualified person to determine if all or part of the Indicated and Measured Mineral Resources may be converted to mineral reserves at the time of reporting. The financial analysis must have the level of detail necessary to demonstrate, at the time of reporting, that extraction is economically viable. A Pre-Feasibility Study is less comprehensive and results in a lower confidence level than a feasibility study. A Pre-Feasibility study is more comprehensive and results in a higher confidence level than an Initial Assessment. title: Neon Rides Shines a Light on Wild Vehicles from the Radwood Era
summary: “What will remain of the 1980s?” That’s the question the Italian pop singer and songwriter Raf, best known for the 1983 hit “Self Control” (you may be familiar with Laura Branigan’s version, which ranked fourth on Billboard’s Top 100 the same year), asked in a single released in Italy in February 1989. Back then, it […]
body_text: “ What will remain of the 1980s? ” That’s the question the Italian pop singer and songwriter Raf, best known for the 1983 hit “Self Control” (you may be familiar with Laura Branigan’s version, which ranked fourth on Billboard’s Top 100 the same year), asked in a single released in Italy in February 1989. Back then, it charted at sixth place among the country’s top singles, and now it’s a charming throwback I enjoy listening to from time to time. It’s not a sad song, but it’s got a melancholic vibe—the message is that little of the decade would stand the test of time. The 1980s had been, according to Raf’s lyrics, vacuous, frivolous years, destined to be forgotten and discarded like empty beer cans. Boy, was he wrong on this one. Mitokino/gestalten/Petersen Automotive Museum Here we are in 2026, and it seems the 1980s have never left . Contemporary pop culture has been imbued with ’80s nostalgia for years, and now that older millennials are approaching middle age, that trend has been rapidly extending to the 1990s. This generational shift is transforming the collector car market in more ways than one, and as an aging millennial myself, I certainly cannot blame anyone for wanting to drop over $100K on the cleanest Lancia Integrale or Supra Twin Turbo. So it was perhaps only natural that Neon Rides , the latest book from the German publishing house Gestalten, caught my eye while I was visiting my favorite local bookstore. Mitokino/gestalten/Petersen Automotive Museum Mitokino/gestalten/Petersen Automotive Museum Mitokino/gestalten/Petersen Automotive Museum Mitokino/gestalten/Petersen Automotive Museum Neon Rides is certainly hard to miss. It’s a chunky beast at 288 pages of thick, high-grade paper, and, since photography takes precedence over text, it also has a suitably large page format, at roughly 12 by 10 inches. It’s the definition of a “coffee table book,” a publication made to impress more than inform. While not the sort of book I tend to buy, much like the vehicles it features, Neon Rides has a certain something that makes it hard to resist. Mitokino/gestalten/Petersen Automotive Museum For starters, it just looks cool. The stitched-bound hardcover is as white as Pablo Escobar’s finest, and, as far as cover cars go, I cannot imagine anything more apt for this than a white-on-white Lamborghini Countach . Not only is it perfectly representative of the era, looking straight off the set of a Miami Vice episode, but it also gives the cover a strikingly minimalist look, as the white of the Lambo’s paint blends with the background. The big, bold, yet elegantly scripted title is off to the right in black, partially hidden by the Countach’s sloping front end. I love it. The book was made in collaboration with the Petersen Automotive Museum in Los Angeles and serves as a partial catalog of sorts for its “Totally Awesome” exhibition, which opened in June 2025 and ran until April this year. The complete list of vehicles and props is provided at the end, but Neon Rides is more of a curated selection—and a pretty solid one at that. The 35 vehicles featured in the book are organized into eight chapters. The opening one, aptly named “Zeitgeist,” features the aforementioned Countach 5000 S, a Lotus Esprit Turbo, and one car that’s the polar opposite of those: the hilariously gaudy Cadillac Seville by Gucci. I have to admit I didn’t know it ever existed, but now I’m glad it does, even if it isn’t my cup of tea. Mitokino/gestalten/Petersen Automotive Museum Speaking of things I didn’t know existed, the “Motorcycles” chapter is the one that brought me the most pinch-me moments, featuring some truly insane contraptions. Like, for example, the Krauser Domani, a wedge-shaped three-wheeler powered by a BMW K1200 inline-four engine. Inspired by racing sidecar technology, it looks like a prop from a period sci-fi flick, and it’s simply glorious! But, as a former automotive designer, the section of Neon Rides that truly did it for me is the second chapter, titled “Looking Forward.” It features some of the most memorable concept cars from the 1980s and ’90s and thus brings me right back to my formative years as a teenager dreaming of drawing cars for a living someday. Cars like the Italdesign Aztec from 1988 or the Ford Indigo from 1996, which are etched in my memory and remind me of a time when the automobile industry still looked resolutely to a future that, to paraphrase another hit song from the 1980s, seemed to look “so bright, I gotta wear shades.” Just as one would expect from a publication of this caliber, the photography is top-notch. The pictures, courtesy of the LA-based media company Mitokino, look fantastic, as the bright white studio setting sets off each vehicle’s design features to great effect. Mitokino/gestalten/Petersen Automotive Museum Yet, what ultimately sold me on Neon Rides has hardly anything to do with the vehicles themselves. I finally decided to close the book and take it to the cashier’s counter after glancing at the non-automotive sections placed between the main chapters, which offer an overview of some of the period’s most significant pop-culture trends. Covering topics from fashion houses like Gucci and Versace to video games like the legendary titles Hang-On and Daytona USA, the content in these sections adds a further layer of meaning and context that is rarely seen in automotive publications, and Neon Rides is all the better for it. Mitokino/gestalten/Petersen Automotive Museum Last, but definitely not least, this is a book that looks and feels far more expensive than the roughly $90 it goes for on Gestalten’s website . Reading Neon Rides won’t make you an expert on anything. In fact, in terms of raw information, you’d be much better off reading the Wikipedia entries for each vehicle. But not all books need to be founts of knowledge. This is a gorgeous-looking paper time machine guaranteed to bring a smile to your face every time you flick through its pages and, for that alone, it’s a worthy addition to any enthusiast’s bookshelf. The post Neon Rides Shines a Light on Wild Vehicles from the Radwood Era appeared first on Hagerty Media .

This guide compares honest alternatives for shops that need jobs on a board this week. TL;DR: Housecall Pro wins solo operators who live on reviews and consumer booking. Taskade Genesis wins small crews who want to own the dispatch system — board, customer history, portal, and follow-up automations in one workspace plan instead of per-tech seats. Jobber wins packaged defaults. Generate a Housecall Pro-style dispatch board → For the broader category see Best AI Ops Dashboard Builders . Here the question is narrower: what replaces Housecall Pro when per-seat cost or schema rigidity starts to hurt? Competitor figures below are public or widely reported ranges as of July 2026. Confirm live quotes before you buy. Field-service vendors repackage tiers and move features between them more often than any other software category on this list. 🧰 What Small Crews Actually Need From Field-Service Software A full field-service management suite promises booking, dispatch, GPS, price books, proposals, payments, review marketing, and reporting. A four-truck shop usually lives in a much narrower week: A customer calls, texts, or books online. Someone puts the job on a board with an address, a window, and a tech. The tech closes it out with notes, photos, and parts used. An estimate turns into an invoice without anyone re-typing a price. Someone asks for the Google review while the job is still fresh. The owner wants one screen that answers "what is open and who owes us money?" That spine is a dispatch board with customer history attached. It is not a marketing suite. Confusing the two is how small crews end up paying for modules nobody opens. Keep your telematics Who configures fields Vendor templates You plus Taskade EVE chat If your week is the six steps above, you are shopping for ownership of the board. If your week is consumer booking widgets, review campaign attribution, and financing offers at the door, a packaged residential suite is genuinely the better buy. 📜 Where the Per-Tech Seat Tax Came From Field-service software grew up solving a real problem: paper work orders lost in truck cabs. Charging per technician made sense when every tech needed a licensed mobile app, when the vendor funded GPS breadcrumbs and a price book, and when the alternative was a clipboard. Three things changed for small crews by 2026: Office staff need write access too. Dispatchers, bookkeepers, and the owner's spouse all touch the schedule. Seat-capped tiers push you up a tier or into per-user add-ons long before you hire a fifth tech. The real system of record is already a group chat. Most shops under ten trucks coordinate in SMS and a spreadsheet. Paying a licensed seat for someone who updates a status twice a day feels like a tax on visibility, not a tool. Generating a custom board got cheap. You can describe a work-order app in plain language and have it deployed the same afternoon, then rename a column without filing a support ticket. That moves the decision from "which residential brand?" to "do we rent a schema or own one?" None of that makes Housecall Pro wrong. Per-seat pricing is a business model matched to packaged depth — someone has to fund the booking widget and the review engine. Crews feel the pinch at a predictable moment: when the features they actually need sit one tier up, or when the sixth hire costs another line item before booking a first job. That loop is what an owned board is built to hold end to end. GPS trails and payment processing are adjacent systems that plug in beside it. 💵 2026 Pricing Reality: Housecall Pro, Jobber, ServiceTitan Treat the table below as a budget sketch, not a contract. Your dispatch today is a spreadsheet plus group chat , and you mainly need triage, assignment, and history. You want fields that match your trade — gate codes, roof zones, panel amperage, filter sizes — without waiting on vendor templates. You already have payments and accounting somewhere you trust and do not want to migrate them. You want AI follow-ups grounded on your own board , not a chatbot that cannot read your schema. Seat quotes keep climbing faster than the revenue the software helped you win. Good fits: two-to-six-truck plumbing, HVAC, and electrical shops; cleaning and landscaping crews with recurring routes; specialty trades with checklists no vendor template covers; property maintenance teams running internal and customer-facing work side by side. It is a strong product aimed at a specific buyer. Stay when that buyer is you: Consumer booking is your funnel. The online booking widget, branded reminders, and homeowner-facing polish are tuned for residential conversion in a way a board you build yourself will not match on day one. Review marketing is your growth engine. Automated review requests wired into a reputation dashboard is a real product, not a checkbox. If Google reviews drive your phone volume, that packaging earns its price. You want payments in the same contract. Card-on-file, financing offers at the door, and payouts inside one product remove a wiring project you may not want. You refuse to configure anything. Some owners want screens that arrive finished. That is a legitimate preference and Housecall Pro respects it. Your techs work in dead zones and you rely on a mature offline mobile app plus GPS breadcrumbs. You are mid-rollout with training sunk and adoption finally sticking. Do not restart a rollout to save $60 a month. Jobber is the closest packaged peer — similar shape, different quoting and payment defaults. ServiceTitan targets larger shops with call centers and dedicated admins; worth a demo only when you already run marketing ops inside an enterprise suite. Small crews rarely need that depth on day one. They run on Workspace DNA — Memory, Intelligence, and Execution feeding each other. Every cycle leaves the board better informed than the last, which is the opposite of a schedule that resets every morning. What you generate first, in order: Jobs as the single source of truth for open work. Customers linked so history survives the job closing. Money stages — quote sent, approved, invoiced, paid — so nothing ages silently. Agents only after the board holds real jobs. An agent on demo rows is theater. If equipment hangs off the job instead of the customer, you lose history the moment the job closes. Model it once and the board answers questions you did not think to ask. Three modeling rules that save you a rebuild: Equipment belongs to the customer, not the job. A twelve-year-old water heater outlives forty service calls. Hang it off the address and every future tech inherits the history. Estimates convert, they do not duplicate. One record moves quote to job to invoice so nobody re-types a price. That is what the estimate to invoice pipeline and job to invoice flow exist for. Recurring agreements are their own record. A maintenance contract is a promise; a visit is a truck roll. Keep them separate with a recurring service agreement tracker so the daily board stays readable. Set the fields up once in table view , then read the same records in board view for dispatch or calendar view for windows. Taskade ships 7 project views — List, Board, Calendar, Table, Mind Map, Gantt, and Org Chart, with Timeline part of Gantt — over the same underlying records, so office staff and techs read the shape that suits them without duplicating data.
